# M3 acceptance report: extraction and normalization

- **Run date:** 2026-11-13
- **Branch:** `m3-extract` (log captured before the M3 commit, on top of `54114ea`)
- **Raw evidence:** [M3_results.log](M3_results.log) — full, unedited command output
- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M3` (about 15 minutes)
- **Needs:** an LLM key. It makes real model calls. It reads the pages M2
  cached, so it fetches no page and makes no search query unless the cache
  is empty.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M3_results.log`.

| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M3 tests | all pass | 99 passed | PASS |
| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 274 passed, 13 deselected (the 13 need keys) | PASS |
| 3 | Real-model tests | all pass | 6 passed | PASS |
| 4 | Accuracy on 5 labelled pages | measured | precision 100%, recall 82% (9 of 11 pairs) | PASS (measured, see section 2) |
| 5 | Campfire, collect and extract | `complete` | `complete`; 20 model calls; 16 claims about 4 people; 5 claims refused | PASS |
| 6 | Campfire again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 16 claims | PASS |
| 7 | Robinhood, collect and extract | `complete` | `complete`; 26 model calls; 70 claims about 25 people; 7 claims refused | PASS |
| 8 | Robinhood again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 70 claims | PASS |
| 9 | Campfire leaders with evidence | listing | 3 current, 2 unverified leader roles | PASS |
| 10 | Robinhood leaders with evidence | listing | 6 current, 7 unverified, 4 former leader roles | PASS |
| 11 | Campfire refused claims | listing | 6 entries, each with its reason | PASS |
| 12 | Robinhood refused claims | listing | 9 entries, each with its reason | PASS |
| 13 | Every stored claim re-checked | 0 problems | 86 claims re-checked against their saved pages, 0 failed; every current role has a supporting claim | PASS |
| 14 | M1 mutation check | all caught | 23 of 23 | PASS |
| 15 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 146 files scanned (86 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |

15 of 15 steps as expected.

No model is faked anywhere. The fast tests either use no model at all or
place a recorded model answer in the extraction cache, which exercises the
real cache-hit path. The six real-model tests and steps 4, 5 and 7 call the
real provider.

## 2. M3 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 100% of stored claims pass the evidence check | Met | Step 13: 86 of 86, re-checked independently of the run |
| Rejected claims logged | Met | Steps 11 and 12; `test_cached_answer_from_either_model_is_reused_and_checked` |
| CEO of each company extracted | Met | John Glasgow (Campfire), Vladimir Tenev (Robinhood), both `current` with canonical role CEO |
| Extraction accuracy measured on labelled pages | Met | Step 4: precision 100%, recall 82% |
| Malformed output handled | Met | `test_real_output_that_fails_validation_is_retried_once_then_the_document_is_skipped` |
| Injection test passes | Met | `test_real_model_does_not_follow_instructions_planted_in_a_page` |
| Resume test passes | Met | `test_real_run_stopped_by_its_limit_resumes_without_repeating_work`; steps 6 and 8 |

**About the 82% recall.** Two of the eleven labelled pairs were missed, both
"the CEO, named as the speaker or host on a page about someone else":

- `campfire-customer-cfo.txt`: the model wrote "Camp**ground**" where the
  page says "Campfire" in its quote. The evidence check refused the claim.
- `robinhood-howard-coo.txt`: the model did not extract Vlad Tenev, who is
  named only in the attribution of a quotation.

The misses differ from run to run: an earlier run missed Tenev on the Pinner
page instead (a bug in my check, since fixed) and found Glasgow. So the
model is not fully repeatable even at temperature 0, mainly because two
different models answer depending on pacing. A misquote costs coverage, not
correctness: nothing wrong was stored on any of the five pages, and no
person from another organisation was stored.

## 3. What was found

**Campfire** (12 documents read, 16 claims, 4 people)

| Status | Person | Title | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| current | John Glasgow | CEO & Founder | listed on the company's own page |
| current | Erik Leavell | Head of Finance & Applied AI | listed on the company's own page |
| current | Chris McDonough | VP of Sales | dated article, September 2026 |
| unverified | John Glasgow | CFO | one undated third-party page ("and still CFO") |
| unverified | Paul Nichols | CTO | one company post from February 2025, older than 12 months |

**Robinhood** (19 documents read, 70 claims, 25 people)

| Status | Person | Title | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| current | Vladimir Tenev | Chair and Chief Executive Officer | SEC filings, 2026 |
| current | Shiv Verma | Chief Financial Officer | SEC filings, 2026 |
| current | Daniel Gallagher | Chief Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs Officer; also Chief Legal Officer | SEC proxy statement, April 2026 |
| current | Steven Quirk | Chief Brokerage Officer | SEC proxy statement |
| current | Dara Bazzano | Chief Accounting Officer | SEC 8-K, June 2026 |
| former | Jeffrey Pinner | Chief Technology Officer | SEC 8-K: separated effective 2026-05-07 |
| former | Jason Warnick | Chief Financial Officer | SEC filing: ceased effective 2026-02-06 |
| former | Shiv Verma | Senior Vice President of Finance and Strategy | SEC filing gives it as his earlier title |
| former | Anne Hoge | Chief Legal Officer | a successor was appointed (rule 3) |
| unverified | Gretchen Howard (COO), Christina Smedley (CMO), Aparna Chennapragada (CPO), Baiju Bhatt (Co-CEO), Norm Ashkenas and Kelly Zigaitis (unit compliance officers) | | only press releases from 2019 to 2021 |

The seven unverified Robinhood roles are the honest result of the rules: a
2020 press release does not show the person still holds the office. Deciding
them is the job of targeted verification in M4.

The second search round did not run for either company (a CEO and at least
three leaders were found), and the log says so.

## 4. Checklist rows covered

| Row | Requirement (short) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R27 | Real LLM, fixed Pydantic schema | Steps 3, 5, 7; `test_schema_rejects_what_the_model_must_not_send` |
| R28 | Evidence check; rejections logged | Step 13; steps 11, 12; four evidence tests |
| R29 | Only the target company | `test_a_title_at_another_organisation_is_rejected`; step 4: 0 outsiders on five pages |
| R30 | Level by rules | `test_level_from_title` (23 cases incl. CEO, SVP, EVP, Head of, Director, board member) |
| R31 | Department from a fixed list | Enforced by the schema; `test_schema_rejects_...` |
| R32 | Canonical role | `test_canonical_role`; both CEOs have canonical role CEO (section 3) |
| R33 | Same person merged by normalized name | `test_people_are_merged_by_normalized_name`; `test_store_document_replaces_...` |
| R34, R99 | Nicknames only with a matching role; near matches flagged | `test_nicknames_merge_only_with_the_same_role_and_near_names_are_flagged`, `test_name_comparison` |
| R70 | Effective date apart from publication date | `test_effective_date_is_stored_apart_...`; Robinhood 8-K filed 2026-06-26, effective 2026-06-25 (labelled page) |
| R71 | Cache keyed on content and extraction version | `test_extraction_version_changes_with_prompt_schema_or_model`; steps 6, 8 |
| R72 | Re-extraction replaces older claims | `test_changed_prompt_re_extracts_and_leaves_no_claim_of_the_old_version` |

- **Branch:** `m3-extract` (log captured before the M3 commit, on top of `54114ea`)
- **Raw evidence:** [M3_results.log](M3_results.log) — full, unedited command output
- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M3` (about 15 minutes)
- **Needs:** an LLM key. It makes real model calls. It reads the pages M2
  cached, so it fetches no page and makes no search query unless the cache
  is empty.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M3_results.log`.

| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M3 tests | all pass | 99 passed | PASS |
| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 274 passed, 13 deselected (the 13 need keys) | PASS |
| 3 | Real-model tests | all pass | 6 passed | PASS |
| 4 | Accuracy on 5 labelled pages | measured | precision 100%, recall 82% (9 of 11 pairs) | PASS (measured, see section 2) |
| 5 | Campfire, collect and extract | `complete` | `complete`; 20 model calls; 16 claims about 4 people; 5 claims refused | PASS |
| 6 | Campfire again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 16 claims | PASS |
| 7 | Robinhood, collect and extract | `complete` | `complete`; 26 model calls; 70 claims about 25 people; 7 claims refused | PASS |
| 8 | Robinhood again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 70 claims | PASS |
| 9 | Campfire leaders with evidence | listing | 3 current, 2 unverified leader roles | PASS |
| 10 | Robinhood leaders with evidence | listing | 6 current, 7 unverified, 4 former leader roles | PASS |
| 11 | Campfire refused claims | listing | 6 entries, each with its reason | PASS |
| 12 | Robinhood refused claims | listing | 9 entries, each with its reason | PASS |
| 13 | Every stored claim re-checked | 0 problems | 86 claims re-checked against their saved pages, 0 failed; every current role has a supporting claim | PASS |
| 14 | M1 mutation check | all caught | 23 of 23 | PASS |
| 15 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 146 files scanned (86 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |

15 of 15 steps as expected.

No model is faked anywhere. The fast tests either use no model at all or
place a recorded model answer in the extraction cache, which exercises the
real cache-hit path. The six real-model tests and steps 4, 5 and 7 call the
real provider.

## 2. M3 acceptance criteria (SPEC section 8)

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 100% of stored claims pass the evidence check | Met | Step 13: 86 of 86, re-checked independently of the run |
| Rejected claims logged | Met | Steps 11 and 12; `test_cached_answer_from_either_model_is_reused_and_checked` |
| CEO of each company extracted | Met | John Glasgow (Campfire), Vladimir Tenev (Robinhood), both `current` with canonical role CEO |
| Extraction accuracy measured on labelled pages | Met | Step 4: precision 100%, recall 82% |
| Malformed output handled | Met | `test_real_output_that_fails_validation_is_retried_once_then_the_document_is_skipped` |
| Injection test passes | Met | `test_real_model_does_not_follow_instructions_planted_in_a_page` |
| Resume test passes | Met | `test_real_run_stopped_by_its_limit_resumes_without_repeating_work`; steps 6 and 8 |

**About the 82% recall.** Two of the eleven labelled pairs were missed, both
"the CEO, named as the speaker or host on a page about someone else":

- `campfire-customer-cfo.txt`: the model wrote "Camp**ground**" where the
  page says "Campfire" in its quote. The evidence check refused the claim.
- `robinhood-howard-coo.txt`: the model did not extract Vlad Tenev, who is
  named only in the attribution of a quotation.

The misses differ from run to run: an earlier run missed Tenev on the Pinner
page instead (a bug in my check, since fixed) and found Glasgow. So the
model is not fully repeatable even at temperature 0, mainly because two
different models answer depending on pacing. A misquote costs coverage, not
correctness: nothing wrong was stored on any of the five pages, and no
person from another organisation was stored.

## 3. What was found

**Campfire** (12 documents read, 16 claims, 4 people)

| Status | Person | Title | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| current | John Glasgow | CEO & Founder | listed on the company's own page |
| current | Erik Leavell | Head of Finance & Applied AI | listed on the company's own page |
| current | Chris McDonough | VP of Sales | dated article, September 2026 |
| unverified | John Glasgow | CFO | one undated third-party page ("and still CFO") |
| unverified | Paul Nichols | CTO | one company post from February 2025, older than 12 months |

**Robinhood** (19 documents read, 70 claims, 25 people)

| Status | Person | Title | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| current | Vladimir Tenev | Chair and Chief Executive Officer | SEC filings, 2026 |
| current | Shiv Verma | Chief Financial Officer | SEC filings, 2026 |
| current | Daniel Gallagher | Chief Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs Officer; also Chief Legal Officer | SEC proxy statement, April 2026 |
| current | Steven Quirk | Chief Brokerage Officer | SEC proxy statement |
| current | Dara Bazzano | Chief Accounting Officer | SEC 8-K, June 2026 |
| former | Jeffrey Pinner | Chief Technology Officer | SEC 8-K: separated effective 2026-05-07 |
| former | Jason Warnick | Chief Financial Officer | SEC filing: ceased effective 2026-02-06 |
| former | Shiv Verma | Senior Vice President of Finance and Strategy | SEC filing gives it as his earlier title |
| former | Anne Hoge | Chief Legal Officer | a successor was appointed (rule 3) |
| unverified | Gretchen Howard (COO), Christina Smedley (CMO), Aparna Chennapragada (CPO), Baiju Bhatt (Co-CEO), Norm Ashkenas and Kelly Zigaitis (unit compliance officers) | | only press releases from 2019 to 2021 |

The seven unverified Robinhood roles are the honest result of the rules: a
2020 press release does not show the person still holds the office. Deciding
them is the job of targeted verification in M4.

The second search round did not run for either company (a CEO and at least
three leaders were found), and the log says so.

## 4. Checklist rows covered

| Row | Requirement (short) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R27 | Real LLM, fixed Pydantic schema | Steps 3, 5, 7; `test_schema_rejects_what_the_model_must_not_send` |
| R28 | Evidence check; rejections logged | Step 13; steps 11, 12; four evidence tests |
| R29 | Only the target company | `test_a_title_at_another_organisation_is_rejected`; step 4: 0 outsiders on five pages |
| R30 | Level by rules | `test_level_from_title` (23 cases incl. CEO, SVP, EVP, Head of, Director, board member) |
| R31 | Department from a fixed list | Enforced by the schema; `test_schema_rejects_...` |
| R32 | Canonical role | `test_canonical_role`; both CEOs have canonical role CEO (section 3) |

| R100 | No tools; text delimited and labelled untrusted | The request in `extract.py`; `test_markers_in_a_page_cannot_close_the_document_block` |

## 5. Errors and issues met during M3

| # | What happened | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The model named people as "Mr. Tenev" and "Ms. Bazzano" | It copied the sentence's wording | A claim needs a given name and a surname; the prompt asks for the full name given elsewhere. The honorific forms are refused and logged |
| 2 | Evidence such as "Director" or "each of our founders..." was accepted for a named person | The check only asked whether the quote was somewhere in the document | The person's surname must be in the quote or within 250 characters of it |
| 3 | Real table rows were refused ("evidence not in the document"), losing Robinhood's chief legal officer | The page text keeps table-cell separators that the model leaves out | Separators are treated as formatting, like whitespace |
| 4 | **Dates were invented.** "since May 2020" came back as 2020-05-01, "since August 2024" as 2024-08-01 | The model completed a month to a day although told not to | A date is kept only when the document writes that exact day; otherwise it is dropped and logged. 3 dates were dropped in the last Robinhood run |
| 5 | A past title was read as current: Shiv Verma's earlier post showed as a current role | The model returned "role" for "Prior to his current position, Mr. Verma had been..." | Prompt rule: a title given as past is a role-scoped departure. He now shows as former in that post |
| 6 | "Dan Gallagher" and "Daniel Gallagher" were two leaders | The same office was spelled with and without a comma, so the roles did not match and the nickname rule did not merge them | Commas and "and" are normalized in the canonical role |
| 7 | "Chief Compliance Officer" of a subsidiary looked like a company-wide office | The title did not carry the unit | A title held in a unit keeps the unit's name and gets no single-holder role |
| 8 | The annual report yielded only its signature page | It refers to the proxy statement for its officers, and my ranking of pieces favoured legal wording | Named offices now count most. The officers are found in the proxy statement |
| 9 | Titles such as "Founder CEO / Co-founder" were not recognised as CEO | A slash was read as naming a division | Fixed; test added |
| 10 | The accuracy run missed the CEO on a page | My proximity check deleted text between quotation marks, and the name stood between two quotations | Fixed; test added |
| 11 | The independent re-check reported 10 false failures | It compared the merged name ("Vladimir Tenev") with pages that write "Vlad Tenev" | The name is now stored as each source wrote it, and the re-check uses that |
| 12 | The model invented a person: "John Locke, CEO" on a Campfire post, and misquoted "Campground" | Model error | Both refused by the evidence check (step 11). This is the check doing its job |
| 13 | Two of my new tests failed on first run | Two runs within one second share a log file, and the tests read the earlier run's lines | The tests read only the lines after the last run start. The shared file itself is harmless |

Issue 4 deserves your attention: without that check the database would have
held plausible-looking dates that no source states.

## 6. Decisions made during M3 that the spec did not fix

Please confirm or change these in manual test MT-3.9.

1. **Extraction is part of `leadership collect`**, in the same run and under
   the same limits. `--no-extract` stops after fetching.
2. **The quote must be near the person's name** (250 characters). New
   requirement R156.
3. **A date must be written in full in the source** to be stored. New
   requirement R157. Month-only dates are lost, not rounded.
4. **A title in a unit of the company** keeps the unit's name and is not a
   company-wide single-holder role. New requirement R158.
5. **The name is stored as each source wrote it**, and
   `tools/check_evidence.py` can re-check every claim. New requirement R159.
6. **R153 is implemented by a page-kind judgment from the model**, applied
   by code: a third-party page judged a profile or directory drops to tier
   4. It can only lower a third-party source. In the final data no page was
   lowered, because the M2 exclusions had already removed such pages.
7. **Long documents are read in part**: at most 3 pieces of 4,500 characters,
   chosen by leadership wording.
8. **Presidents and general counsels are C-level.** Directors, board members
   and founders without an office are stored as `other`, outside the scope.
9. **Location and bio are not extracted in M3** beyond a location the page
   states outright. Enrichment is M4.
10. **Two version stamps.** The model answer is cached by prompt, schema and
    model. A change to the checks or rules re-processes documents from that
    cache with no model call.
11. **A run with no LLM key ends `insufficient_data`**, saying no people
    could be extracted.
12. **Three database columns were added**: `sources.extraction_version`,
    `sources.page_kind`, `people.possible_duplicate_of`, and
    `claims.person_as_written`. Older databases get them on opening.

## 7. Not covered in M3

- **Verification of unverified and conflicting roles** (M4). Seven
  Robinhood and two Campfire leader roles wait for it.
- **Location and biography** (M4), and the export of fixtures (M4).
- **Gold-set precision and recall of the whole pipeline** (M4). M3 measures
  five pages only.
- **Robinhood's VPs and Heads.** None was found: the sources read are
  filings and appointment announcements, which name officers.
- **Near-duplicate people.** Two are flagged and kept separate ("Dan
  Gallagher" and "Vlad Tenev", each holding only a board or founder
  mention). Nothing merges them automatically.
- **The invented-URL case of link selection** (M2) is still untested.
- **Groq's daily request limit** is still not counted locally.

## 8. Manual acceptance tests

Run these in a terminal opened in the project folder (PowerShell). Only
MT-3.6 makes model calls.

- [ ] **MT-3.1 Fast tests.** Run `uv run pytest`.
  Expected: last line reads `274 passed, 13 deselected`.

- [ ] **MT-3.2 Campfire leaders.** Run `uv run python tools/show_people.py meetcampfire.com`.
  Expected: John Glasgow as current CEO, and the five rows of section 3.
  For each role, read the quoted evidence and decide whether it supports the
  title. Open one or two of the URLs to compare.

- [ ] **MT-3.3 Robinhood leaders.** Run `uv run python tools/show_people.py robinhood.com`.
  Expected: the rows of section 3. Check in particular Jeffrey Pinner
  (former, with an 8-K quote giving 2026-05-07) and Jason Warnick (former,
  2026-02-06). Decide whether any `current` role looks wrong.

- [ ] **MT-3.4 Refused claims.** Run
  `uv run python tools/show_people.py meetcampfire.com --rejected` and the same
  for `robinhood.com`.
  Expected: 6 and 9 entries, each with a reason. Decide whether any refused
  claim should have been kept.

- [ ] **MT-3.5 Evidence re-check.** Run `uv run python tools/check_evidence.py`.
  Expected: last line reads `86 claims checked: 0 problems`.

- [ ] **MT-3.6 Accuracy.** Run `uv run leadership eval`.
  Expected: precision 100%. Recall may be 82% or 91%, since the model does
  not always miss the same pair. No "person from another organisation".

- [ ] **MT-3.7 Nothing repeats.** Run `uv run leadership collect https://robinhood.com/`.
  Expected: `Status: complete`, `llm_calls 0`, `network calls 0`, and
  "search round 2: not needed".

- [ ] **MT-3.8 The labels.** Open `fixtures/labelled/labels.json` and one of
  the five text files beside it. Check that my hand labels are right: they
  are what the 82% is measured against.

- [ ] **MT-3.9 Decisions.** Read section 6 and confirm or change each of the
  twelve decisions.

- [ ] **MT-3.10 Checklist.** In `SPEC_checklist.xlsx`, filter Milestone to
  `M3` and review the Status and Notes.

## 9. Open questions for you

1. **Is 82% recall on the labelled pages acceptable for M3?** The spec asks
   that it be measured, not that it reach a number. The whole-pipeline
   thresholds (precision 90%, gold C-level recall 100%) are checked in M4.
2. **Unverified Robinhood officers.** Seven are unverified because the only
   sources are old. M4's verification search is designed for this. Say if
   you want anything done about them before M4.

"""One-off patch: checklist for M3, and one wording fix in the report."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "acceptance" / "M3.md"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = "12. **Three database columns were added**:"
assert s.count(old) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(old, "12. **Four database columns were added**:"), encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

path = root / "SPEC_checklist.xlsx"
wb = load_workbook(path)
ws = wb["Requirements"]
old_last = ws.max_row
while ws.cell(row=old_last, column=1).value is None:
    old_last -= 1
BUILT = "Built 2026-11-13. Evidence: acceptance/M3.md section 4"
NOTES = {
    "R21": "Pages, search, link-pick and extraction answers are all cached (M3 acceptance steps 6, 8). Complete; awaiting M3 sign-off",
    "R83": "Built 2026-11-13. Not triggered for either company; the run says so. Evidence: acceptance/M3.md section 4",
    "R84": "Both halves built: budget stop (M2) and at most one extra search round (M3). Awaiting M3 sign-off",
    "R94": BUILT + ". No company-scoped departure occurs in the two companies' data",
    "R98": "Built 2026-11-13. Precision 100%, recall 82% (9 of 11 pairs). acceptance/M3.md section 2",
    "R102": "Measured 2026-11-13: scripts and comments are dropped; text hidden by a style is kept. Documented in SPEC 6.5 and README",
    "R153": "Built 2026-11-13 as a page-kind judgment applied by code (tier 3 -> tier 4). No page was lowered in the final data. acceptance/M3.md section 6",
}
n = 0
for r in range(2, old_last + 1):
    rid, ms, status = (ws.cell(row=r, column=c).value for c in (1, 5, 8))
    if ms == "M3" and status == "Not started":
        ws.cell(row=r, column=8).value = "In progress"
        ws.cell(row=r, column=9).value = NOTES.get(rid, BUILT)
        n += 1
    elif rid in ("R21", "R84"):
        ws.cell(row=r, column=9).value = NOTES[rid]
print("M3 rows set to In progress:", n)
NEW = [
 ("Extraction", "The evidence quote must be about the person it is attached to: their surname is in the quote or within 250 characters of it",
  "Unit tests with a real sentence attached to the wrong person, and with a name between two quotations", "3.3"),
 ("Extraction", "An effective date is stored only when the source writes that exact day; a date the model completed from a month or year is dropped and logged",
  "Unit tests on date wording; run log shows dropped dates for Robinhood", "3.3"),
 ("Extraction", "A title held in one unit of the company keeps the unit's name and is not a company-wide single-holder role",
  "Unit tests; Robinhood's two unit compliance officers have no canonical role", "3.3, 3.4"),
 ("Extraction", "Each claim keeps the person's name as its source wrote it, and every stored claim can be re-checked against its saved page without a model",
  "tools/check_evidence.py reports 0 problems on all stored claims", "3.3, 4"),
]
for i, (area, req, check, sec) in enumerate(NEW, 1):
    r = old_last + i
    vals = [f"R{r - 1:02d}", area, req, "P0", "M3", check, sec, "In progress",
            "Built 2026-11-13. Evidence: acceptance/M3.md sections 5 and 6"]
    for c, v in enumerate(vals, 1):
        src = ws.cell(row=old_last, column=c)
        cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=c, value=v)
        cell.font, cell.border = copy.copy(src.font), copy.copy(src.border)
        cell.fill, cell.alignment = copy.copy(src.fill), copy.copy(src.alignment)
new_last = old_last + len(NEW)


def bump(ref):
    return re.sub(rf"(\$?[A-I]\$?){old_last}\b", rf"\g<1>{new_last}", ref)


ws.auto_filter.ref = bump(ws.auto_filter.ref)
for dv in ws.data_validations.dataValidation:
    dv.sqref = type(dv.sqref)(bump(str(dv.sqref)))
new_cf = ConditionalFormattingList()
for cf in ws.conditional_formatting:
    for rule in cf.rules:
        new_cf.add(bump(str(cf.sqref)), rule)
ws.conditional_formatting = new_cf
for sheet in wb.worksheets:
    if sheet.title == "Requirements":
        continue
    for row in sheet.iter_rows():
        for cell in row:
            if isinstance(cell.value, str) and cell.value.startswith("="):
                cell.value = cell.value.replace(f"${old_last},", f"${new_last},").replace(f"${old_last})", f"${new_last})")
wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("rows", old_last, "->", new_last, "| new ids", f"R{old_last}..R{new_last - 1}")

"""One-off patch: record the answers of 2026-11-13 and carry two items into M4."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "acceptance" / "M3.md"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
start = s.index("## 9. Open questions for you")
end = s.index("## 10. Sign-off")
new = '''## 9. Questions

Answered by you on 2026-11-13:

1. **82% recall on the labelled pages is accepted for M3**, on condition
   that the missed CEO cases are documented (section 2) and carried into M4
   for improvement. Carried as checklist row R160: a leader named only as
   the speaker of a quotation, the host or the author must be extracted, and
   the five pages are measured again.
2. **The seven unverified Robinhood officers stay `unverified`.** Their
   status is not guessed. Only evidence found by M4's verification may
   change it.
3. **M4 must check VP and Head coverage explicitly**, because Robinhood has
   none. Carried as checklist row R161: the M4 report states, per company,
   how many VPs and Heads are in the gold set and how many were found, and
   says so plainly when none is found.

Nothing is open.

'''
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:], encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

path = root / "SPEC_checklist.xlsx"
wb = load_workbook(path)
ws = wb["Requirements"]
old_last = ws.max_row
while ws.cell(row=old_last, column=1).value is None:
    old_last -= 1
NEW = [
 ("Extraction", "A leader of the company named only as the speaker of a quotation, as the host or as the author is extracted; "
  "the five labelled pages are measured again and the result compared with M3 (recall 82%, two CEO misses)",
  "P0", "`leadership eval`: both CEO pairs missed in M3 are found, or the M4 report explains why not", "3.3, 7.2",
  "Carried from M3 on 2026-11-13 as a condition of accepting 82% recall. See acceptance/M3.md section 2"),
 ("Verification", "VP and Head coverage is checked explicitly: per company, the gold set lists VPs and Heads, and the report "
  "states how many were found; zero found is reported as a gap, not passed over",
  "P0", "M4 report has a VP and Head coverage table for each company", "7.2, 7.4",
  "Asked for on 2026-11-13: M3 found no VP or Head for Robinhood"),
]
for i, (area, req, pri, check, sec, note) in enumerate(NEW, 1):
    r = old_last + i
    vals = [f"R{r - 1:02d}", area, req, pri, "M4", check, sec, "Not started", note]
    for c, v in enumerate(vals, 1):
        src = ws.cell(row=old_last, column=c)
        cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=c, value=v)
        cell.font, cell.border = copy.copy(src.font), copy.copy(src.border)
        cell.fill, cell.alignment = copy.copy(src.fill), copy.copy(src.alignment)
new_last = old_last + len(NEW)


def bump(ref):
    return re.sub(rf"(\\$?[A-I]\\$?){old_last}\\b", rf"\\g<1>{new_last}", ref)


ws.auto_filter.ref = bump(ws.auto_filter.ref)
for dv in ws.data_validations.dataValidation:
    dv.sqref = type(dv.sqref)(bump(str(dv.sqref)))
new_cf = ConditionalFormattingList()
for cf in ws.conditional_formatting:
    for rule in cf.rules:
        new_cf.add(bump(str(cf.sqref)), rule)
ws.conditional_formatting = new_cf
for sheet in wb.worksheets:
    if sheet.title == "Requirements":
        continue
    for row in sheet.iter_rows():
        for cell in row:
            if isinstance(cell.value, str) and cell.value.startswith("="):
                cell.value = cell.value.replace(f"${old_last},", f"${new_last},").replace(f"${old_last})", f"${new_last})")
wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("rows", old_last, "->", new_last, ws.auto_filter.ref)

"""Investigate four reported issues in the stored Robinhood data. Reads only."""
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

c = sqlite3.connect(Path(sys.argv[1]) / "data" / "leadership.db")
c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
cid = c.execute("SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain = 'robinhood.com'").fetchone()[0]


def show(title, sql, args=()):
    print("\n==", title)
    for r in c.execute(sql, args):
        print("  ", {k: (str(r[k])[:170] if r[k] is not None else None) for k in r.keys()})


CL = """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.claim_type, cl.departure_scope AS scope, cl.raw_title, cl.canonical_role AS canon,
        cl.as_of_date, cl.as_of_basis AS basis, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.effective_pending AS pend, s.tier,
        s.source_type AS st, substr(s.url, -48) AS url, cl.evidence
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
        WHERE cl.company_id = ? AND {} ORDER BY p.full_name, cl.id"""
RO = """SELECT p.full_name, r.title, r.status, r.status_reason, r.ended_on, r.ended_by_claim_id, r.first_seen,
        r.last_seen, r.supporting_claim_id FROM roles r JOIN people p ON p.id = r.person_id
        WHERE r.company_id = ? AND {} ORDER BY p.full_name"""
for name in ("Warnick", "Hoge"):
    show(f"{name}: claims", CL.format("p.full_name LIKE ?"), (cid, f"%{name}%"))
    show(f"{name}: roles", RO.format("p.full_name LIKE ?"), (cid, f"%{name}%"))
show("Verma SVP: claims", CL.format("p.full_name LIKE '%Verma%' AND cl.raw_title LIKE '%Senior%'"), (cid,))
show("Verma: roles", RO.format("p.full_name LIKE '%Verma%'"), (cid,))
show("claims with an effective date on the 1st of a month (all companies)",
     """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.raw_title, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.as_of_date, substr(s.url, -40) AS url, cl.evidence
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
        WHERE cl.effective_date LIKE '%-01'""")
show("all effective dates stored", """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.claim_type, cl.raw_title, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.as_of_date
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id WHERE cl.effective_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cl.id""")
show("roles whose first_seen or ended_on falls on the 1st of a month",
     RO.format("(r.first_seen LIKE '%-01' OR r.ended_on LIKE '%-01')"), (cid,))
show("Gallagher / Quirk / Verma CFO roles", RO.format("(p.full_name LIKE '%Gallagher%' OR p.full_name LIKE '%Quirk%')"), (cid,))

import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

c = sqlite3.connect(Path(sys.argv[1]) / "data" / "leadership.db")
c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
cid = c.execute("SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain = 'robinhood.com'").fetchone()[0]


def show(title, sql, args=()):
    print("\n==", title)
    for r in c.execute(sql, args):
        print("  ", {k: (str(r[k])[:170] if r[k] is not None else None) for k in r.keys()})


CL = """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.claim_type, cl.departure_scope AS scope, cl.raw_title, cl.canonical_role AS canon,
        cl.as_of_date, cl.as_of_basis AS basis, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.effective_pending AS pend, s.tier,
        s.source_type AS st, substr(s.url, -48) AS url, cl.evidence
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
        WHERE cl.company_id = ? AND {} ORDER BY p.full_name, cl.id"""
RO = """SELECT p.full_name, r.title, r.status, r.status_reason, r.ended_on, r.ended_by_claim_id, r.first_seen,
        r.last_seen, r.supporting_claim_id FROM roles r JOIN people p ON p.id = r.person_id
        WHERE r.company_id = ? AND {} ORDER BY p.full_name"""
for name in ("Warnick", "Hoge"):
    show(f"{name}: claims", CL.format("p.full_name LIKE ?"), (cid, f"%{name}%"))
    show(f"{name}: roles", RO.format("p.full_name LIKE ?"), (cid, f"%{name}%"))
show("Verma SVP: claims", CL.format("p.full_name LIKE '%Verma%' AND cl.raw_title LIKE '%Senior%'"), (cid,))
show("Verma: roles", RO.format("p.full_name LIKE '%Verma%'"), (cid,))
show("claims with an effective date on the 1st of a month (all companies)",
     """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.raw_title, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.as_of_date, substr(s.url, -40) AS url, cl.evidence
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id
        WHERE cl.effective_date LIKE '%-01'""")
show("all effective dates stored", """SELECT cl.id, p.full_name, cl.claim_type, cl.raw_title, cl.effective_date AS eff, cl.as_of_date
        FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id WHERE cl.effective_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cl.id""")
show("roles whose first_seen or ended_on falls on the 1st of a month",
     RO.format("(r.first_seen LIKE '%-01' OR r.ended_on LIKE '%-01')"), (cid,))
show("Gallagher / Quirk / Verma CFO roles", RO.format("(p.full_name LIKE '%Gallagher%' OR p.full_name LIKE '%Quirk%')"), (cid,))

dates on plain role claims; narrow backstops for 'leaving later this month' wording."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:60], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

"""One-off patch: no end date unless a source states it; dates checked next to the quote; no
dates on plain role claims; narrow backstops for 'leaving later this month' wording."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:60], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

"""One-off patch: M3 report and checklist after the review corrections."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "acceptance" / "M3.md"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
pairs = [
 ("- **Run date:** 2026-11-13\n",
  "- **Run date:** 2026-11-13 (rerun the same day after your review found four faults in the stored dates; section 5, issues 14 to 18)\n"),
 ("- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M3` (about 15 minutes)",
  "- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M3` (15 minutes when the provider is not rate-limiting; the last run took 90 minutes, nearly all of it the real-model tests waiting on the free-tier limit)"),
 ("| 1 | M3 tests | all pass | 99 passed | PASS |", "| 1 | M3 tests | all pass | 103 passed | PASS |"),
 ("| 274 passed, 13 deselected (the 13 need keys) | PASS |", "| 287 passed, 13 deselected (the 13 need keys) | PASS |"),
 ("| `complete`; 20 model calls; 16 claims about 4 people; 5 claims refused | PASS |",
  "| `complete`; 16 claims about 4 people; 5 claims refused; 3 current leaders, 1 unverified person not counted. 0 model calls in this rerun: the prompt did not change, so the cached answers were re-processed | PASS |"),
 ("| 6 | Campfire again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 16 claims | PASS |",
  "| 6 | Campfire again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 16 claims, no document touched | PASS |"),
 ("| `complete`; 26 model calls; 70 claims about 25 people; 7 claims refused | PASS |",

 ("| 8 | Robinhood again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 70 claims | PASS |",
  "| 8 | Robinhood again | 0 model calls | 0 model calls, 0 network calls, same 67 claims | PASS |"),
 ("| 86 claims re-checked against their saved pages, 0 failed; every current role has a supporting claim | PASS |",
  "| 83 claims re-checked against their saved pages, 0 failed; every current role has a supporting claim | PASS |"),
 ("| 146 files scanned (86 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |", "| 154 files scanned (92 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |"),
 ("| 100% of stored claims pass the evidence check | Met | Step 13: 86 of 86, re-checked independently of the run |",
  "| 100% of stored claims pass the evidence check | Met | Step 13: 83 of 83, re-checked independently of the run |"),
 ("**Robinhood** (19 documents read, 70 claims, 25 people)", "**Robinhood** (19 documents read, 67 claims, 25 people)"),
 ("| former | Jason Warnick | Chief Financial Officer | SEC filing: ceased effective 2026-02-06 |",
  "| former | Jason Warnick | Chief Financial Officer | SEC 8-K dated 2026-02-10 says he \"has transitioned to an advisory role\". **End date not stored**: see below |"),
 ("| former | Shiv Verma | Senior Vice President of Finance and Strategy | SEC filing gives it as his earlier title |",
  "| former | Shiv Verma | Senior Vice President of Finance and Strategy | SEC filings give it as his earlier title. End date not stated, so none is stored |"),
 ("| former | Anne Hoge | Chief Legal Officer | a successor was appointed (rule 3) |",
  "| former | Anne Hoge | Chief Legal Officer | a later source shows her successor in office (rule 3). End date not stated, so none is stored |"),
 ('''The seven unverified Robinhood roles are the honest result of the rules:''',
  '''**Jason Warnick's end date.** The proxy statement says he "ceased to serve
as Chief Financial Officer effective February 6, 2026". The model read that
passage but did not return that sentence in the stored run; it returned only
the 8-K's "has transitioned to an advisory role", which gives no date. So the
database holds no end date for him, with "reported by a source dated
2026-02-10". It no longer shows 2026-02-10 as the day he left. Recovering
2026-02-06 needs the model to return that sentence, which is part of R160
in M4. I did not copy the date from his successor's appointment, because
that would be a date no source states about him.

The seven unverified Robinhood roles are the honest result of the rules:'''),
 ('''Issue 4 deserves your attention: without that check the database would have
held plausible-looking dates that no source states.''',
  '''| 14 | **Found by you.** Jason Warnick's CFO role ended on 2026-02-10 in the database; the source says 2026-02-06 | When a departure had no stated date, the rules used the filing date as the end date | An end date is now only ever a date a source states. Otherwise `ended_on` is empty and a new field, `end_reported_on`, holds the date of the reporting source. Six regression tests, one of them over all 45 worked cases |
| 15 | **Found by you.** "since January 2022" and "since February 2026" were stored as 2022-01-01 and 2026-02-01, despite issue 4's fix | My check looked for the date anywhere in the document. The 363,000-character proxy contains "January 1, 2022" in a share-plan paragraph and "February 1, 2026" in a vesting footnote | The date must be in the quote or within 250 characters of it. Also, a plain `role` claim no longer carries any date. No stored claim has a first-of-month date now |
| 16 | **Found by you.** Shiv Verma's earlier title had an end date the evidence does not establish | Same cause as issue 14 | Fixed by issue 14: `former`, no end date |
| 17 | **Found by you.** Anne Hoge's departure used the announcement date although the page says "leaving Robinhood later this month" | The model did not mark the departure as still to come, and the rules then used the announcement date | A quote that describes an undated change as still to come now marks it pending, in code. Her role is `former` because a later source shows her successor in office, with no end date |
| 18 | Signature dates on the annual report were stored as effective dates of eleven roles | The model put the signing date into `effective_date` | Covered by issue 15: role claims carry no date |

Issues 14 to 17 were mine to catch and I did not: my first fix for invented
dates (issue 4) was too weak, and I had not looked at where end dates came
from. Without your review the database would have shown four dates that no
source states.'''),
 ('''3. **A date must be written in full in the source** to be stored. New
   requirement R157. Month-only dates are lost, not rounded.''',
  '''3. **A date must be written in full, next to the quote**, to be stored. New
   requirement R157. Month-only dates are lost, not rounded. Only
   appointments and departures carry a date.
3a. **An end date is only a date a source states** (R162). A role can be
   `former` with no end date; the date of the reporting source is kept
   apart in `end_reported_on`.
3b. **Unverified people are counted apart from current leaders** (R163), in
   the run report, the counters and the second-search trigger.'''),
 ("  Expected: last line reads `274 passed, 13 deselected`.", "  Expected: last line reads `287 passed, 13 deselected`."),
 ('''  Expected: the rows of section 3. Check in particular Jeffrey Pinner
  (former, with an 8-K quote giving 2026-05-07) and Jason Warnick (former,
  2026-02-06). Decide whether any `current` role looks wrong.''',
  '''  Expected: the rows of section 3. Check in particular Jeffrey Pinner
  (former, "ended on 2026-05-07", with the 8-K quote), and Jason Warnick,
  Anne Hoge and Shiv Verma's earlier title (each former, "end date not
  stated", with the date of the reporting source). Decide whether any
  `current` role looks wrong.'''),
 ("  Expected: last line reads `86 claims checked: 0 problems`.", "  Expected: last line reads `83 claims checked: 0 problems`."),
 ('''  Expected: `Status: complete`, `llm_calls 0`, `network calls 0`, and
  "search round 2: not needed".''',
  '''  Expected: `Status: complete`, `llm_calls 0`, `network calls 0`,
  "search round 2: not needed", and the line
  `Current leaders: 5. Unverified, not counted as current: 6`.'''),
 ("- [ ] **MT-3.9 Decisions.** Read section 6 and confirm or change each of the\n  twelve decisions.",
  "- [ ] **MT-3.9 Decisions.** Read section 6 and confirm or change each of the\n  fourteen decisions (twelve, plus 3a and 3b)."),
]
for old, new in pairs:
    assert s.count(old) == 1, (old[:70], s.count(old))
    s = s.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

path = root / "SPEC_checklist.xlsx"
wb = load_workbook(path)
ws = wb["Requirements"]
old_last = ws.max_row
while ws.cell(row=old_last, column=1).value is None:
    old_last -= 1
done = 0
for r in range(2, old_last + 1):
    if ws.cell(row=r, column=1).value == "R157":
        ws.cell(row=r, column=3).value = (
            "An effective date is stored only when the source writes that exact day in the evidence quote or within "
            "250 characters of it; a date the model completed, or one found elsewhere in the document, is dropped and "
            "logged. Only appointments and departures carry a date")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=6).value = ("Unit tests incl. a date 100,000 characters from the quote; no stored claim has a "
                                          "first-of-month date; no role claim has a date")
        ws.cell(row=r, column=9).value = ("Built 2026-11-13; tightened the same day after review (acceptance/M3.md "
                                          "section 5, issues 15 and 18)")
        done += 1
assert done == 1
NEW = [
 ("Verification", "A role's end date is only ever a date a source states. Without one the role is former with no end date, "
  "and the date of the source that reported the end is kept in a separate field",
  "Six rule tests, one over all 45 worked cases; Robinhood: Warnick, Hoge and Verma's earlier title have no end date",
  "3.6, 4", "Found in review 2026-11-13. acceptance/M3.md section 5, issues 14, 16, 17"),
 ("Verification", "Unverified roles are never returned or counted as current leaders: the current-leadership view, the run "
  "counters and the second-search trigger use current roles only",
  "Database and pipeline tests; run report line 'Current leaders: N. Unverified, not counted as current: M'",
  "3.6, 3.10", "Confirmed and made explicit 2026-11-13 at your request"),
]
for i, (area, req, check, sec, note) in enumerate(NEW, 1):
    r = old_last + i
    vals = [f"R{r - 1:02d}", area, req, "P0", "M3", check, sec, "In progress", note]
    for c, v in enumerate(vals, 1):
        src = ws.cell(row=old_last, column=c)
        cell = ws.cell(row=r, column=c, value=v)
        cell.font, cell.border = copy.copy(src.font), copy.copy(src.border)
        cell.fill, cell.alignment = copy.copy(src.fill), copy.copy(src.alignment)
new_last = old_last + len(NEW)


def bump(ref):
    return re.sub(r"(\$?[A-I]\$?)" + str(old_last) + r"\b", r"\g<1>" + str(new_last), ref)


ws.auto_filter.ref = bump(ws.auto_filter.ref)
for dv in ws.data_validations.dataValidation:
    dv.sqref = type(dv.sqref)(bump(str(dv.sqref)))
new_cf = ConditionalFormattingList()
for cf in ws.conditional_formatting:
    for rule in cf.rules:
        new_cf.add(bump(str(cf.sqref)), rule)
ws.conditional_formatting = new_cf
for sheet in wb.worksheets:
    if sheet.title == "Requirements":
        continue
    for row in sheet.iter_rows():
        for cell in row:
            if isinstance(cell.value, str) and cell.value.startswith("="):
                cell.value = cell.value.replace(f"${old_last},", f"${new_last},").replace(f"${old_last})", f"${new_last})")
wb.properties.lastModifiedBy = ""
wb.properties.creator = ""
wb.save(path)
print("rows", old_last, "->", new_last, ws.auto_filter.ref)

All four faults you found are fixed, with 13 regression tests, and the full M3 acceptance reran 15 of 15 on the corrected code. The corrections are not committed; the earlier M3 commit on `m3-extract` still has the faulty behaviour.

You were right on every point. I checked each against the saved pages.

| # | What you found | Cause | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Warnick's CFO role ended 2026-02-10 | With no stated date, the rules used the filing date as the end date | `former`, end date empty, "reported by a source dated 2026-02-10" |
| 2 | "since January 2022" stored as 2022-01-01 | My date check searched the whole document; the proxy has "January 1, 2022" in a share-plan paragraph | No stored claim has a first-of-month date |
| 3 | Verma's earlier title had an unsupported end date | Same cause as 1 | `former`, end date empty |
| 4 | Hoge's departure used the announcement date | The model did not mark "leaving later this month" as still to come | `former` because a later source shows her successor in office; end date empty |

## What changed

- **End dates:** a role's end date is only ever a date a source states. Otherwise it is empty, and a separate field holds the date of the source that reported the end.
- **Date check:** a date must be written in the quote or within 250 characters of it.
- **Role claims carry no date.** Only appointments and departures do. This also removed eleven signature dates that had been stored as effective dates.
- **Changes still to come:** "is leaving later this month" and "will be joining" are marked pending in code. "Will remain employed until…" is deliberately not matched.

## Warnick's date is empty, not 2026-02-06

The proxy does say he "ceased to serve as Chief Financial Officer effective February 6, 2026". The model read that passage but did not return that sentence in the stored run. So the database now holds no end date for him. Recovering it needs the model to return that sentence, which belongs with the recall work already carried into M4 (R160). I did not copy the date from his successor's appointment, since no source states that date about him.

## Unverified roles

They cannot be treated as current leaders:

- **The view of current leaders** returns `current` roles only; a new test checks this with an old press release.
- **The run report** now prints them apart: Robinhood shows "Current leaders: 5. Unverified, not counted as current: 6".
- **The second-search trigger** used to count unverified people toward "enough leaders found". It now counts current leaders only.

## Rerun results

- **Fast tests:** 287 passed.
- **Real-model tests:** 6 passed. They took 90 minutes this time because of free-tier rate limits.
- **Evidence re-check:** 83 of 83 claims pass. The count fell from 86 because duplicate claims that differed only by a dropped date were merged.
- **Accuracy on labelled pages:** unchanged at 100% precision, 82% recall.
- **Both companies:** `complete` with 0 model calls, since the prompt did not change and cached answers were re-processed.

[acceptance/M3.md](acceptance/M3.md) has these as issues 14 to 18, with updated expectations for your manual tests (MT-3.1 now expects `287 passed`, MT-3.5 expects 83 claims). [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) is revision 11, and the checklist has two new rows, R162 and R163.

Say when you want these corrections committed and pushed to `m3-extract`.

"""One-off patch: documentation and checklist only, before M3 sign-off."""
import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:60], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


patch("acceptance/M3.md", [
 ('''- **Needs:** an LLM key. It makes real model calls. It reads the pages M2
  cached, so it fetches no page and makes no search query unless the cache
  is empty.''',
  '''- **Needs:** an LLM key. It reads the pages M2 cached, so it fetches no page
  and makes no search query unless the cache is empty. How many real model
  calls it makes depends on what is already cached: see "Real provider calls
  and cached answers" in section 1.'''),
 ('''No model is faked anywhere. The fast tests either use no model at all or
place a recorded model answer in the extraction cache, which exercises the
real cache-hit path. The six real-model tests and steps 4, 5 and 7 call the
real provider.
''', '''### Real provider calls and cached answers

No model is faked anywhere. But in the final run recorded in the log, most
steps were answered from the cache, and I should not describe those as real
calls. The split is:

| Step | In the final run (this log) | Where its model answers came from |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 Fast tests | no provider call | No model, or a recorded answer placed in the cache by the test |
| 3 Real-model tests | **real provider calls** | Each test uses an empty temporary cache, so every answer is fresh |
| 4 Accuracy on labelled pages | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from a run earlier the same day (7 real calls at that time) |
| 5 Campfire | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:46 the same day, which made 20 real calls |
| 6 Campfire again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do: every document already extracted |
| 7 Robinhood | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:49 the same day, which made 26 real calls |
| 8 Robinhood again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do |

So the stored claims for both companies do come from the real model, but
from calls made earlier on 2026-11-13, with the same prompt, schema and
models. The final run re-processed those answers with the corrected checks
and rules. Its log shows `llm_calls 0` for steps 5 and 7, which is correct
for that run and is not evidence of fresh calls. The earlier calls are in
`logs/collect-meetcampfire.com-20261113T014631.jsonl` and
`logs/collect-robinhood.com-20261113T014948.jsonl` (not committed). A run on
a machine with an empty cache would make those calls again, and could return
slightly different claims, because the model is not fully repeatable.
'''),
 ('''## 7. Not covered in M3
''', '''## 7. Known limitations and what M3 does not cover

### Limitations of what was built

- **Extraction recall: a stated date can be missed (Jason Warnick).** The
  proxy statement says he "ceased to serve as Chief Financial Officer
  effective February 6, 2026". The passage was sent to the model, but the
  model did not return that sentence, so no claim carries the date. The
  database therefore shows his CFO role as `former` with **no end date**
  and "reported by a source dated 2026-02-10". This is a recall limitation
  of extraction, not a rule decision: the date exists in a source we hold
  and we did not capture it. Nothing in M3 detects such a miss. Recovering
  explicitly stated dates is M4 requirement R164.
- **The 250-character evidence window.** The quote must have the person's
  surname, and any effective date, in it or within 250 characters. This is
  a fixed distance, not an understanding of the text. It can wrongly accept
  a quote that sits near a different person with the same surname, or a
  date nearby that belongs to another event. It can wrongly refuse a
  correct claim when a long paragraph puts the name or the date more than
  250 characters from the quote, or when a later sentence uses only "he" or
  "she". Refusals are logged; wrong acceptances are not detectable by the
  tool.
- **Long documents are read in part.** At most three pieces of 4,500
  characters are sent to the model, chosen by counting leadership wording.
  Robinhood's proxy statement has 88 pieces and its annual report 174, so
  about 3% and 2% of them are read. A relevant passage that scores low is
  never seen. The choice is by keywords, so it can prefer a signature page
  to a paragraph that states a departure. Which pieces were read is not
  recorded per claim.
- **The C-level convention.** "C-level" here means: any "Chief ... Officer"
  title or its abbreviation, any President who is not a Vice President, and
  a General Counsel. That is a convention I chose, not a standard. It makes
  "Chief Accounting Officer" and "Chief Brokerage Officer" C-level, and also
  the chief officer of a single unit ("Chief Compliance Officer, Robinhood
  Financial"), who is C-level by title but not a company-wide officer. It
  excludes "Chief of Staff", founders without an office, chairs and board
  members, and "Managing Director". Counts of C-level leaders, and the M4
  gold-set recall for C-level, depend on this convention.

### Not covered in M3
'''),
 ('''Nothing is open.

## 10. Sign-off''', '''4. **Stated dates must be recovered** (asked for on 2026-11-13). Carried as
   a separate M4 requirement, R164: when a source we hold states the full
   effective date of an appointment or departure, the stored claim carries
   it. Jason Warnick's 2026-02-06 is the test case.

Nothing is open.

## 10. Sign-off

Left for your approval. Nothing below is filled in, and the M3 checklist
rows stay In progress until you sign off.'''),

import copy
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.formatting.formatting import ConditionalFormattingList

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:60], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

 ('''- **Needs:** an LLM key. It makes real model calls. It reads the pages M2
  cached, so it fetches no page and makes no search query unless the cache
  is empty.''',

  calls it makes depends on what is already cached: see "Real provider calls
  and cached answers" in section 1.'''),

place a recorded model answer in the extraction cache, which exercises the
real cache-hit path. The six real-model tests and steps 4, 5 and 7 call the
real provider.

steps were answered from the cache, and I should not describe those as real
calls. The split is:

| Step | In the final run (this log) | Where its model answers came from |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 Fast tests | no provider call | No model, or a recorded answer placed in the cache by the test |
| 3 Real-model tests | **real provider calls** | Each test uses an empty temporary cache, so every answer is fresh |
| 4 Accuracy on labelled pages | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from a run earlier the same day (7 real calls at that time) |
| 5 Campfire | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:46 the same day, which made 20 real calls |
| 6 Campfire again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do: every document already extracted |
| 7 Robinhood | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:49 the same day, which made 26 real calls |
| 8 Robinhood again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do |

from calls made earlier on 2026-11-13, with the same prompt, schema and
models. The final run re-processed those answers with the corrected checks
and rules. Its log shows `llm_calls 0` for steps 5 and 7, which is correct
for that run and is not evidence of fresh calls. The earlier calls are in
`logs/collect-meetcampfire.com-20261113T014631.jsonl` and
`logs/collect-robinhood.com-20261113T014948.jsonl` (not committed). A run on
a machine with an empty cache would make those calls again, and could return
slightly different claims, because the model is not fully repeatable.
'''),
 ('''## 7. Not covered in M3
''', '''## 7. Known limitations and what M3 does not cover

### Limitations of what was built

- **Extraction recall: a stated date can be missed (Jason Warnick).** The
  proxy statement says he "ceased to serve as Chief Financial Officer
  effective February 6, 2026". The passage was sent to the model, but the
  model did not return that sentence, so no claim carries the date. The
  database therefore shows his CFO role as `former` with **no end date**
  and "reported by a source dated 2026-02-10". This is a recall limitation
  of extraction, not a rule decision: the date exists in a source we hold
  and we did not capture it. Nothing in M3 detects such a miss. Recovering
  explicitly stated dates is M4 requirement R164.
- **The 250-character evidence window.** The quote must have the person's
  surname, and any effective date, in it or within 250 characters. This is
  a fixed distance, not an understanding of the text. It can wrongly accept
  a quote that sits near a different person with the same surname, or a
  date nearby that belongs to another event. It can wrongly refuse a
  correct claim when a long paragraph puts the name or the date more than
  250 characters from the quote, or when a later sentence uses only "he" or
  "she". Refusals are logged; wrong acceptances are not detectable by the
  tool.
- **Long documents are read in part.** At most three pieces of 4,500
  characters are sent to the model, chosen by counting leadership wording.
  Robinhood's proxy statement has 88 pieces and its annual report 174, so
  about 3% and 2% of them are read. A relevant passage that scores low is
  never seen. The choice is by keywords, so it can prefer a signature page
  to a paragraph that states a departure. Which pieces were read is not
  recorded per claim.
- **The C-level convention.** "C-level" here means: any "Chief ... Officer"
  title or its abbreviation, any President who is not a Vice President, and
  a General Counsel. That is a convention I chose, not a standard. It makes
  "Chief Accounting Officer" and "Chief Brokerage Officer" C-level, and also
  the chief officer of a single unit ("Chief Compliance Officer, Robinhood
  Financial"), who is C-level by title but not a company-wide officer. It
  excludes "Chief of Staff", founders without an office, chairs and board
  members, and "Managing Director". Counts of C-level leaders, and the M4
  gold-set recall for C-level, depend on this convention.

### Not covered in M3
'''),

 ('''- **Needs:** an LLM key. It makes real model calls. It reads the pages M2
  cached, so it fetches no page and makes no search query unless the cache
  is empty.''',
  '''- **Needs:** an LLM key. It reads the pages M2 cached, so it fetches no page
  and makes no search query unless the cache is empty. How many real model
  calls it makes depends on what is already cached: see "Real provider calls
  and cached answers" in section 1.'''),
 ('''No model is faked anywhere. The fast tests either use no model at all or
place a recorded model answer in the extraction cache, which exercises the
real cache-hit path. The six real-model tests and steps 4, 5 and 7 call the
real provider.
''', '''### Real provider calls and cached answers

No model is faked anywhere. But in the final run recorded in the log, most
steps were answered from the cache, and I should not describe those as real
calls. The split is:

| Step | In the final run (this log) | Where its model answers came from |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 Fast tests | no provider call | No model, or a recorded answer placed in the cache by the test |
| 3 Real-model tests | **real provider calls** | Each test uses an empty temporary cache, so every answer is fresh |
| 4 Accuracy on labelled pages | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from a run earlier the same day (7 real calls at that time) |
| 5 Campfire | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:46 the same day, which made 20 real calls |
| 6 Campfire again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do: every document already extracted |
| 7 Robinhood | 0 provider calls | Cached answers from the run at 01:49 the same day, which made 26 real calls |
| 8 Robinhood again | 0 provider calls | Nothing to do |

So the stored claims for both companies do come from the real model, but
from calls made earlier on 2026-11-13, with the same prompt, schema and
models. The final run re-processed those answers with the corrected checks
and rules. Its log shows `llm_calls 0` for steps 5 and 7, which is correct
for that run and is not evidence of fresh calls. The earlier calls are in
`logs/collect-meetcampfire.com-20261113T014631.jsonl` and
`logs/collect-robinhood.com-20261113T014948.jsonl` (not committed). A run on
a machine with an empty cache would make those calls again, and could return
slightly different claims, because the model is not fully repeatable.
'''),
 ('''## 7. Not covered in M3
''', '''## 7. Known limitations and what M3 does not cover

### Limitations of what was built

- **Extraction recall: a stated date can be missed (Jason Warnick).** The
  proxy statement says he "ceased to serve as Chief Financial Officer
  effective February 6, 2026". The passage was sent to the model, but the
  model did not return that sentence, so no claim carries the date. The
  database therefore shows his CFO role as `former` with **no end date**
  and "reported by a source dated 2026-02-10". This is a recall limitation
  of extraction, not a rule decision: the date exists in a source we hold
  and we did not capture it. Nothing in M3 detects such a miss. Recovering
  explicitly stated dates is M4 requirement R164.
- **The 250-character evidence window.** The quote must have the person's
  surname, and any effective date, in it or within 250 characters. This is
  a fixed distance, not an understanding of the text. It can wrongly accept
  a quote that sits near a different person with the same surname, or a
  date nearby that belongs to another event. It can wrongly refuse a
  correct claim when a long paragraph puts the name or the date more than

  the chief officer of a single unit ("Chief Compliance Officer, Robinhood
  Financial"), who is C-level by title but not a company-wide officer. It
  excludes "Chief of Staff", founders without an office, chairs and board
  members, and "Managing Director". Counts of C-level leaders, and the M4
  gold-set recall for C-level, depend on this convention.

### Not covered in M3
'''),
 ('''Nothing is open.

def check_claim(claim: ExtractedClaim, text: str, target: Target) -> str | None:
    """Why a claim must be rejected, or None. No model is involved."""
    plain = squash(text)
    quote = squash(claim.evidence).strip('"').strip()
    if len(quote) < 8 or quote not in plain:
        return "the evidence quote is not in the document"
    name = normalize_name(claim.person).split()
    if len(name) < 2:
        return "the person is not named in full (given name and surname)"
    if squash(claim.person).casefold() not in plain.casefold():
        return "the person's name is not in the document"
    # The quote must be about this person: their surname is in it or right next to it.
    lowered, surname, at, near = _plain_lower(plain), name[-1], -1, False
    while (at := lowered.find(_plain_lower(quote), at + 1)) != -1 and not near:
        near = surname in lowered[max(0, at - NEAR_CHARS):at + len(quote) + NEAR_CHARS]
    if not near:
        return "the evidence quote is not about this person (their name is not near it)"
    if organisation_relation(claim.organization, target) == "other":
        return f"the title is at another organisation ({claim.organization[:60]})"
    return None


def date_is_stated(iso: str, text: str) -> bool:
def extract_document(llm: LLM, target: Target, text: str, *, source_type: str, doc_date: str | None,
                     url: str, max_chunks: int, cache: FileCache, log: RunLog,
                     take_call=lambda: True) -> DocResult:
    """Extract and check the claims of one document. Raises ProviderDown, Malformed or OverBudget."""
    result = DocResult()
    text = text.replace("<<<DOCUMENT", "").replace("DOCUMENT>>>", "")    # the markers are ours alone
    kinds: list[str] = []
    for piece in chunks(text, max_chunks):
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": USER.format(
                company=target.name, domains=", ".join(sorted(target.domains)),
                description=target.description or "unknown", source_type=source_type,
                doc_date=doc_date or "not stated", departments=", ".join(DEPARTMENTS),
                max_claims=MAX_CLAIMS_PER_CHUNK, text=piece)},
        ]
        parsed, version, calls = _ask(llm, messages, cache, log, url, take_call)
        result.calls += calls
        result.versions.add(version)
        kinds.append(parsed.page_kind)
        if not parsed.about_target_company:
            result.about_target = False
            log.event("document_rejected", url=url, claims=len(parsed.claims),
                      reason="the model judged the document to be about another organisation")
            for c in parsed.claims:
                result.rejected.append((c, "the model judged the document to be about another organisation"))
            continue
        for c in parsed.claims:
            reason = check_claim(c, text, target)
            if reason:
                result.rejected.append((c, reason))
                log.event("claim_rejected", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                          claim_type=c.claim_type, reason=reason)
                continue
            if c.effective_date and not date_is_stated(c.effective_date, around(c.evidence, text)):
                # The model completed "since May 2020" into a day. A date is kept only
                # when the source states it in full in, or right next to, the quote.
                # Looking anywhere in the document is not enough: a long filing has
                # "January 1, 2022" somewhere for unrelated reasons.
                log.event("date_dropped", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                          effective_date=c.effective_date,
                          reason="the source does not state this date in full next to the quote")
                result.dates_dropped += 1
                c.effective_date = None
            if c.claim_type in ("appointment", "departure") and not c.effective_date:
                if not c.effective_pending and _FUTURE.search(squash(c.evidence)):
                    # "is leaving later this month", "will be joining": not yet done when written.
                    c.effective_pending = True
                    log.event("pending_set", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                              reason="the quote describes the change as still to come, with no date")
            if (c.claim_type == "departure" and c.departure_scope == "role"
                    and _leaves_company(squash(c.evidence), target)):
                c.departure_scope = "company"
            whole_company = organisation_relation(c.organization, target) == "company"
            if (not whole_company and c.raw_title
                    and squash(c.organization).casefold() not in squash(c.raw_title).casefold()):
                # "Chief Compliance Officer" of one unit must not read as the company's.
                c.raw_title = f"{c.raw_title.strip()}, {squash(c.organization)}"[:200]
            result.accepted.append(Accepted(
                claim=c, version=version, level=level(c.raw_title),
                canonical_role=canonical_role(c.raw_title, target.name) if whole_company else None))
    if kinds:
        result.page_kind = max(set(kinds), key=kinds.count)
    return result

115	   - "departure": the person is leaving or has left ("steps down", "former CTO").
116	     "departure_scope" is "role" if they leave the title, "company" if they leave the company.
117	   - "location": where the person is based, only if the document says so. Put it in "value".
118	   A title the document gives as past ("previously", "prior to", "formerly", "had been",
119	   "served as ... until") is a "departure" with scope "role", never a "role".
120	   A move from one title to another is two claims: a role-scoped departure and an appointment.
121	   A person with two offices ("CEO and CFO") gets one claim per office.
122	4. "raw_title": the title as written, without the company name.
123	5. "department": one of {departments}.
124	6. "effective_date": the date the change takes or took effect, as YYYY-MM-DD, only if the
125	   document states the full date with its day. "since May 2020" or "in 2024" is not a full
126	   date: use null. Never complete a date and never use the document date for it.
127	7. "effective_pending": true only when the document describes the change as still in the
128	   future and gives no date ("will become CFO", "plans to step down").
129	8. "evidence": one sentence or phrase copied from the document exactly, character for
130	   character, that states this fact. At most 300 characters.
131	9. "person": the full name (given name and surname) exactly as the document writes it. If a
132	   sentence says "Mr. Smith" or "she", use the full name the document gives elsewhere. If the
133	   document never gives the full name, skip the person.
134	10. "page_kind": "official" for the company's own page, filing or press release; "article" for
135	    original reporting or an interview by a publisher; "profile_or_directory" for a third-party
136	    listing, database entry, company profile or compiled summary of people; else "other".
137	11. If the document names no leader of the target company, return an empty "claims" list.
138	    At most {max_claims} claims.
139

def check_claim(claim: ExtractedClaim, text: str, target: Target) -> str | None:
    """Why a claim must be rejected, or None. No model is involved."""
    plain = squash(text)
    quote = squash(claim.evidence).strip('"').strip()
    if len(quote) < 8 or quote not in plain:
        return "the evidence quote is not in the document"
    name = normalize_name(claim.person).split()
    if len(name) < 2:
        return "the person is not named in full (given name and surname)"
    if squash(claim.person).casefold() not in plain.casefold():
        return "the person's name is not in the document"
    # The quote must be about this person: their surname is in it or right next to it.
    lowered, surname, at, near = _plain_lower(plain), name[-1], -1, False
    while (at := lowered.find(_plain_lower(quote), at + 1)) != -1 and not near:
        near = surname in lowered[max(0, at - NEAR_CHARS):at + len(quote) + NEAR_CHARS]
    if not near:
        return "the evidence quote is not about this person (their name is not near it)"
    if organisation_relation(claim.organization, target) == "other":
        return f"the title is at another organisation ({claim.organization[:60]})"
    return None

def extract_document(llm: LLM, target: Target, text: str, *, source_type: str, doc_date: str | None,
                     url: str, max_chunks: int, cache: FileCache, log: RunLog,
                     take_call=lambda: True) -> DocResult:
    """Extract and check the claims of one document. Raises ProviderDown, Malformed or OverBudget."""
    result = DocResult()
    text = text.replace("<<<DOCUMENT", "").replace("DOCUMENT>>>", "")    # the markers are ours alone
    kinds: list[str] = []
    for piece in chunks(text, max_chunks):
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
            {"role": "user", "content": USER.format(
                company=target.name, domains=", ".join(sorted(target.domains)),
                description=target.description or "unknown", source_type=source_type,
                doc_date=doc_date or "not stated", departments=", ".join(DEPARTMENTS),
                max_claims=MAX_CLAIMS_PER_CHUNK, text=piece)},
        ]
        parsed, version, calls = _ask(llm, messages, cache, log, url, take_call)
        result.calls += calls
        result.versions.add(version)
        kinds.append(parsed.page_kind)
        if not parsed.about_target_company:
            result.about_target = False
            log.event("document_rejected", url=url, claims=len(parsed.claims),
                      reason="the model judged the document to be about another organisation")
            for c in parsed.claims:
                result.rejected.append((c, "the model judged the document to be about another organisation"))
            continue
        for c in parsed.claims:
            reason = check_claim(c, text, target)
            if reason:
                result.rejected.append((c, reason))
                log.event("claim_rejected", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                          claim_type=c.claim_type, reason=reason)
                continue
            if c.effective_date and not date_is_stated(c.effective_date, around(c.evidence, text)):
                # The model completed "since May 2020" into a day. A date is kept only
                # when the source states it in full in, or right next to, the quote.
                # Looking anywhere in the document is not enough: a long filing has
                # "January 1, 2022" somewhere for unrelated reasons.
                log.event("date_dropped", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                          effective_date=c.effective_date,
                          reason="the source does not state this date in full next to the quote")
                result.dates_dropped += 1
                c.effective_date = None
            if c.claim_type in ("appointment", "departure") and not c.effective_date:
                if not c.effective_pending and _FUTURE.search(squash(c.evidence)):
                    # "is leaving later this month", "will be joining": not yet done when written.
                    c.effective_pending = True
                    log.event("pending_set", url=url, person=c.person, title=c.raw_title,
                              reason="the quote describes the change as still to come, with no date")
            if (c.claim_type == "departure" and c.departure_scope == "role"
                    and _leaves_company(squash(c.evidence), target)):
                c.departure_scope = "company"
            whole_company = organisation_relation(c.organization, target) == "company"
            if (not whole_company and c.raw_title
                    and squash(c.organization).casefold() not in squash(c.raw_title).casefold()):
                # "Chief Compliance Officer" of one unit must not read as the company's.
                c.raw_title = f"{c.raw_title.strip()}, {squash(c.organization)}"[:200]
            result.accepted.append(Accepted(
                claim=c, version=version, level=level(c.raw_title),
                canonical_role=canonical_role(c.raw_title, target.name) if whole_company else None))
    if kinds:
        result.page_kind = max(set(kinds), key=kinds.count)
    return result
