"""One-off patch (M4): the title must be tied to this person, not merely present in the quote."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "leadership" / "extract.py"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = '''    if (claim.claim_type in ("role", "appointment", "departure") and claim.raw_title
            and not states_title(claim.raw_title, quote)
            and not _title_beside_name(claim.raw_title, surname, lowered, _plain_lower(quote))):
        return "neither the evidence quote nor the words beside the person's name state the title"
    return None


BESIDE_CHARS = 60
'''
new = '''    if claim.claim_type in ("role", "appointment", "departure") and claim.raw_title:
        low_quote = _plain_lower(quote)
        by_pronoun = (surname not in low_quote and _PRONOUN.search(low_quote)
                      and states_title(claim.raw_title, low_quote))
        if not by_pronoun and not _title_beside_name(claim.raw_title, surname, lowered, low_quote):
            return "the title is not tied to this person (not in the same sentence as their name)"
    return None


BESIDE_CHARS = 150
# A quote without the name may still be about the person: "She is our Chief Executive Officer."
_PRONOUN = re.compile(r"\\b(?:he|she|his|her|him|hers)\\b")
'''
assert s.count(old) == 1
s = s.replace(old, new)
old2 = '''    """The title stands within BESIDE_CHARS of the surname, close to the quote.

    This accepts the speaker of a quotation: '"...", said Vlad Tenev, CEO and
    Co-Founder'. It refuses a name that merely appears in the same paragraph
    as someone else's title.
    """'''
new2 = '''    """The title stands in the same sentence as the surname, within BESIDE_CHARS, close to the quote.

    This accepts the speaker of a quotation: '"...", said Vlad Tenev, CEO and
    Co-Founder'. It refuses a name that merely appears near someone else's
    title, even when that title is inside the quote: "... Jack Zhang,
    Co-Founder & CEO at AirWallex. ... partner with Accel and John Locke".
    """'''
assert s.count(old2) == 1
s = s.replace(old2, new2)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

t = root / "tests" / "test_extract.py"
s = t.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
pairs = [
 ('''    assert reason == "neither the evidence quote nor the words beside the person's name state the title"''',
  '''    assert reason == "the title is not tied to this person (not in the same sentence as their name)"
    # Even when the quote contains a title, if that title belongs to someone else in it.
    with_title = _claim(person="John Locke", raw_title="CEO",
                        evidence="we have raised a Series A, led by Accel, with support from prominent "
                                 "executives including Jack Zhang, Co-Founder & CEO at AirWallex")
    assert check_claim(with_title, page, ACME) == reason'''),
]
for old, new in pairs:
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:50]
    s = s.replace(old, new)
s += '''

def test_a_quote_without_the_name_needs_a_pronoun_and_the_title():
    page = ("Ada Lovelace joined Acme Robotics in 2019. She is our Chief Executive Officer. "
            "We are proud of our Chief Executive Officer and the whole team.")
    by_pronoun = _claim(evidence="She is our Chief Executive Officer.")
    assert check_claim(by_pronoun, page, ACME) is None
    no_link = _claim(evidence="We are proud of our Chief Executive Officer and the whole team.")
    assert check_claim(no_link, page, ACME) is not None     # no name in its sentence, no pronoun
'''
t.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("patched")

"""One-off patch (M4): sentence ends that are abbreviations; a given name can link a title too."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
p = root / "leadership" / "extract.py"
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
start = s.index("    if claim.claim_type in (\"role\", \"appointment\", \"departure\") and claim.raw_title:\n        low_quote")
end = s.index("def relocate_evidence(")
new = '''    if claim.claim_type in ("role", "appointment", "departure") and claim.raw_title:
        low_quote = _plain_lower(quote)
        by_pronoun = (surname not in low_quote and _PRONOUN.search(low_quote)
                      and states_title(claim.raw_title, low_quote))
        if not by_pronoun and not _title_beside_name(claim.raw_title, name, plain, quote):
            return "the title is not tied to this person (not in the same sentence as their name)"
    return None


BESIDE_CHARS = 150
# A quote without the name may still be about the person: "She is our Chief Executive Officer."
_PRONOUN = re.compile(r"\\b(?:he|she|his|her|him|hers)\\b")
# The end of a sentence: a full stop that does not belong to "Inc.", "Dr." and the like.
_SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"(?<!\\binc)(?<!\\bdr)(?<!\\bmr)(?<!\\bms)(?<!\\bmrs)(?<!\\bcorp)(?<!\\bco)(?<!\\bltd)"
                           r"(?<!\\bjr)(?<!\\bsr)(?<!\\bst)(?<!\\bno)[.!?]\\s", re.I)


def _strip_accents(text: str) -> str:
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
    return "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch))


def _title_beside_name(title: str, name: list[str], plain: str, quote: str) -> bool:
    """The title stands in the same sentence as the person's name, within BESIDE_CHARS, close to the quote.

    This accepts the speaker of a quotation ('"...", said Vlad Tenev, CEO and
    Co-Founder') and a sentence that uses the given name alone ("Since joining
    as Vice President of Operations, Gretchen's leadership ..."). It refuses a
    name that merely appears near someone else's title, even when that title
    is inside the quote: "... Jack Zhang, Co-Founder & CEO at AirWallex. ...
    partner with Accel and John Locke". A given name followed by a different
    surname ("John Glasgow" for John Locke) is another person.
    """
    kept, wanted = _strip_accents(plain), _strip_accents(quote).lower()
    low = kept.lower()
    given, surname = name[0], name[-1]
    at = -1
    while (at := low.find(wanted, at + 1)) != -1:
        start, end = max(0, at - NEAR_CHARS), at + len(wanted) + NEAR_CHARS
        spots = [start + m.start() for m in re.finditer(rf"\\b{re.escape(surname)}\\b", low[start:end])]
        if len(given) >= 3:
            for m in re.finditer(rf"\\b{re.escape(given)}\\b", low[start:end]):
                a = start + m.end()
                follows = re.match(r"(?:['\\u2019]s)?\\s+([A-Z][A-Za-z'\\-]+)", kept[a:a + 40])
                if not follows or follows.group(1).lower() == surname:
                    spots.append(start + m.start())
        for a in spots:
            # Only within the name's own sentence: a signature that follows the
            # sentence, or a title that ends the one before, belongs to someone else.
            before = _SENTENCE_END.split(low[max(0, a - BESIDE_CHARS):a])[-1]
            after = _SENTENCE_END.split(low[a:a + BESIDE_CHARS])[0]
            if states_title(title, before + after):
                return True
    return False


'''
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")

t = root / "tests" / "test_extract.py"
s = t.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
s += '''

def test_abbreviations_do_not_end_the_sentence_that_ties_a_title_to_a_name():
    page = "We are excited to announce Dr. Naomi Boyd has joined Acme Robotics, Inc. as our Chief Economic Advisor."
    boyd = _claim(person="Naomi Boyd", claim_type="appointment", raw_title="Chief Economic Advisor", evidence=page)
    assert check_claim(boyd, page, ACME) is None


def test_a_given_name_alone_can_tie_a_title_but_not_someone_elses_given_name():
    page = ("Gretchen Howard has been elevated to COO of Acme Robotics. Since joining in January as Vice President "
            "of Operations, Gretchen's leadership has expanded to more areas.")
    earlier = _claim(person="Gretchen Howard", raw_title="Vice President of Operations",
                     evidence="Since joining in January as Vice President of Operations, Gretchen's leadership "
                              "has expanded to more areas.")
    assert check_claim(earlier, page, ACME) is None
    two_johns = ("John Glasgow is the CEO of Acme Robotics. It is a chance to partner again with Accel and "
                 "John Locke, after our shared journey.")
    locke = _claim(person="John Locke", raw_title="CEO", evidence="John Glasgow is the CEO of Acme Robotics.")
    assert check_claim(locke, two_johns, ACME) is not None      # "John Glasgow" is not John Locke
'''

questions.question: The spec says the gold set (the hand-verified list of each company's real leaders) must be written from primary sources before the first full pipeline run, so recall is not circular. Who should write the gold sets for Campfire and Robinhood?

options.label: I write them (Recommended)
options.description: You fill in a template I prepare (name, title, level, current or former, source URL) from primary sources such as the SEC proxy and company pages. I hold the verification run until you are done. This keeps the measurement independent of the pipeline.

options.label: Claude drafts, I verify
options.description: I draft both lists from primary sources and you check every row. Faster, but not independent: I have already seen the pipeline's output, and the report would say so.

options.label: Claude writes them
options.description: I write both lists and you do not review them. Fastest, and the weakest evidence: precision and recall would then be measured against my own list.

"""Every line of Campfire's own cached pages that names a title beside 'Campfire' or a blog author."""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
from leadership.sources.web import clean_text  # noqa: E402

seen = Counter()
where = {}
for f in (root / "cache" / "pages").glob("*"):
    try:
        e = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception:
        continue
    key = e.get("key") or ""
    if "campfire.ai" not in key or "thecampfire" in key or "robots" in key or "sitemap" in key:
        continue
    body = (e["value"] or {}).get("body") or ""
    text = clean_text(body) + "\n" + re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"(?s)<[^>]+>", "\n", body))
    for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)\s*(?:\n|,|-|•|·|\|)?\s*((?:Head of|VP|Vice President|Chief|CEO|CTO|CFO|COO|CMO|Co-?[Ff]ounder|Founder|Director of|GM)[^\n|]{0,60}?)(?:,| at| @)?\s*Campfire", text):
        k = (m.group(1), re.sub(r"\s+", " ", m.group(2)).strip(" ,"))
        seen[k] += 1
        where.setdefault(k, key)
    for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)\s*[•·\-–|]\s*((?:Head of|VP|Vice President|Chief|CEO|CTO|Product|Founder)[A-Za-z &,]{0,40})\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December) \d", text):
        k = (m.group(1), "[blog author] " + m.group(2).strip())
        seen[k] += 1
        where.setdefault(k, key)
for (name, title), n in sorted(seen.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(f"{n:>3}  {name:<22}{title[:60]:<62}{where[(name, title)][-60:]}".encode("ascii", "replace").decode())

"""Every line of Campfire's own cached pages that names a title beside 'Campfire' or a blog author."""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
from leadership.sources.web import clean_text  # noqa: E402

seen = Counter()
where = {}
for f in (root / "cache" / "pages").glob("*"):
    try:
        e = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception:
        continue
    key = e.get("key") or ""
    if "campfire.ai" not in key or "thecampfire" in key or "robots" in key or "sitemap" in key:
        continue
    body = (e["value"] or {}).get("body") or ""
    text = clean_text(body) + "\n" + re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"(?s)<[^>]+>", "\n", body))
    for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)\s*(?:\n|,|-|\u2022|\u00b7|\|)?\s*((?:Head of|VP|Vice President|Chief|CEO|CTO|CFO|COO|CMO|Co-?[Ff]ounder|Founder|Director of|GM)[^\n|]{0,60}?)(?:,| at| @)?\s*Campfire", text):
        k = (m.group(1), re.sub(r"\s+", " ", m.group(2)).strip(" ,"))
        seen[k] += 1
        where.setdefault(k, key)
    for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-zA-Z]+)\s*[\u2022\u00b7\-\u2013|]\s*((?:Head of|VP|Vice President|Chief|CEO|CTO|Product|Founder)[A-Za-z &,]{0,40})\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December) \d", text):
        k = (m.group(1), "[blog author] " + m.group(2).strip())
        seen[k] += 1
        where.setdefault(k, key)
for (name, title), n in sorted(seen.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(f"{n:>3}  {name:<22}{title[:60]:<62}{where[(name, title)][-60:]}".encode("ascii", "replace").decode())

content.text:
M4 is partly built on the branch `m4-verify`, and I've drafted the two gold sets for you to verify. The verification search run has not been made, as you chose, and nothing is committed.

## What is built so far

- **Carried from M3:**
  - R165: a first-party page is never refused on the model's "another organisation" judgment alone.
  - R160: the prompt gives examples for quote speakers, hosts and signatures, and a misquoted role is recovered from the page's own sentence.
  - R164: a date that a held source states is recovered without a model.
- **Accuracy on the five labelled pages:** now 100% precision and 100% recall (11 of 11), up from 82%.
- **Verification and enrichment:** written and unit-tested, not yet run for real.
- **Tests:** 307 fast tests pass.

## A fault the re-extraction exposed

After the prompt change, an investor named on Campfire's Series A post (John Locke of Accel) was stored as a Campfire CEO. The model attached a genuine quote that never ties the title to him. The new check requires the title to be in the same sentence as the person's name, or the quote to refer to them by pronoun. He is now refused, with regression tests.

## Gold-set drafts for your review

Both files say they are not independent of the pipeline, since I had already seen its output; I wrote them from the sources' own text.

**Robinhood** ([robinhood.com.json](fixtures/gold/robinhood.com.json)), from SEC filings:

| Person | Title | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vladimir Tenev | Chairman and CEO | current | proxy, April 2026 |
| Shiv Verma | Chief Financial Officer | current, since 2026-02-06 | 8-K, June 2026 |
| Steven Quirk | Chief Brokerage Officer | current | proxy |
| Daniel Gallagher | Chief Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs Officer | current | proxy |
| Dara Bazzano | Chief Accounting Officer | current | 8-K, June 2026 |
| Jason Warnick | Chief Financial Officer | former, ended 2026-02-06 | proxy |
| Jeffrey Pinner | Chief Technology Officer | former, ended 2026-05-07 | 8-K, May 2026 |

**Campfire** ([meetcampfire.com.json](fixtures/gold/meetcampfire.com.json)), from its own pages:

| Person | Title | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| John Glasgow | CEO & Founder | current | conference page |
| Erik Leavell | Head of Finance & Applied AI | current | conference page |
| Brendan Doyle | Head of Product | current | blog author line, 2026-09-18 |

Brendan Doyle is not in the pipeline's output, so this gold set already shows a coverage gap.

## Open items I could not settle from primary sources

1. **Robinhood VPs and Heads:** none is named in any SEC filing held. The company's leadership page refuses the tool, so please open `investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership` and tell me which VPs or Heads to add.
2. **Robinhood's current CTO:** no source names a successor to Pinner.
3. **Is Tenev also President?** The annual report's signature reads "Chief Executive Officer, President, and Director".
4. **Six Robinhood officers known only from 2019 to 2021 press releases** (Howard, Smedley, Chennapragada, Bhatt, Ashkenas, Zigaitis): add any as current or former if you know from a primary source.
5. **Campfire, Chris McDonough (VP of Sales):** named only by a third-party interview. Count him?
6. **Campfire, Paul Nichols (CTO):** named by a company post from February 2025 only. Still CTO?
7. **Campfire, John Glasgow as CFO:** one third-party page says "and still CFO". Count it?

Once you confirm or correct the rows and answer these, I'll mark the gold sets verified, then run verification, enrichment, export and the measurement, followed by the held-out run on Wise.

from leadership.normalize import canonical_role, level  # noqa: E402

DISCLOSURE = ("Not fully blind to earlier pipeline results. The spec asks for a gold set written before any "
              "pipeline output is seen. These annotations were drafted on 2026-11-13, after the M2 and M3 runs, by "
              "someone who had seen their output, and revised the same day on the project owner's corrections. "
              "Every row is taken from the text of a primary source, not from the database, and each row carries "
              "the source and the words it rests on.")
LP = "leadership_page"
PAGE = [  # name, title exactly as the page writes it, business unit named in the title (or None)
    ("Vlad Tenev", "Chairman & Chief Executive Officer", None),

     "Robinhood Financial and Robinhood Securities"),
    ("Taylor Brown", "Chief of Staff", None),

    ("Dan Gallagher", "Chief Legal, Compliance and Corporate Affairs Officer", None),

"""Write the revised gold-set drafts. Levels are computed with the project's own title rules."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
from leadership.normalize import canonical_role, level  # noqa: E402

DISCLOSURE = ("Not fully blind to earlier pipeline results. The spec asks for a gold set written before any "
              "pipeline output is seen. These annotations were drafted on 2026-11-13, after the M2 and M3 runs, by "
              "someone who had seen their output, and revised the same day on the project owner's corrections. "
              "Every row is taken from the text of a primary source, not from the database, and each row carries "
              "the source and the words it rests on.")
LP = "leadership_page"
PAGE = [  # name, title exactly as the page writes it, business unit named in the title (or None)
    ("Vlad Tenev", "Chairman & Chief Executive Officer", None),
    ("Pooja Anand", "Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Audit", None),
    ("Robb Baldwin", "Vice President and General Manager, TradePMR", "TradePMR"),
    ("Matt Billings", "Vice President, Brokerage and President, Robinhood Financial and Robinhood Securities",
     "Robinhood Financial and Robinhood Securities"),
    ("Taylor Brown", "Chief of Staff", None),
    ("Nora Chan", "Senior Director, Communications", None),
    ("Abhishek Fatehpuria", "Vice President, Product Management", None),
    ("Dan Gallagher", "Chief Legal, Compliance and Corporate Affairs Officer", None),
    ("Stephanie Guild", "Chief Investment Officer", None),
    ("Johann Kerbrat", "Senior Vice President and General Manager, Crypto and International", "Crypto and International"),
    ("Chris Koegel", "Vice President, Corporate Finance & Investor Relations", None),
    ("Walter Koller", "Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Robinhood Financial", "Robinhood Financial"),
    ("Seok Lee", "Vice President, Total Rewards", None),
    ("JB Mackenzie", "Vice President and General Manager, Futures and Prediction Markets", "Futures and Prediction Markets"),
    ("Evan McHenry", "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer", None),
    ("Ravi Mehta", "Vice President, Credit Cards and Chief Credit Officer", "Credit Cards"),
    ("Lucas Moskowitz", "Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary", None),
    ("Carley Olivas", "Senior Director, Brand Marketing and Marketing Operations", None),
    ("Steve Quirk", "Chief Brokerage Officer", None),
    ("Deepak Rao", "Senior Vice President and General Manager, Robinhood Money, Robinhood Gold, Growth, and Marketing",
     "Robinhood Money, Robinhood Gold, Growth, and Marketing"),
    ("Connie Schan", "Chief People Officer", None),
    ("Jordan Sinclair", "President of Robinhood UK and General Manager of Bitstamp UK", "Robinhood UK; Bitstamp UK"),
    ("Shiv Verma", "Chief Financial Officer", None),
    ("Nicola White", "Vice President, Institutional Crypto, General Manager, Bitstamp", "Institutional Crypto; Bitstamp"),
]
ALSO = {"Vlad Tenev": ["Vladimir Tenev"], "Dan Gallagher": ["Daniel Gallagher"], "Steve Quirk": ["Steven Quirk"],
        "Stephanie Guild": ["Stephanie Guild, CFA"]}
SEC_QUOTES = {
    "Vlad Tenev": ("proxy", "Vladimir Tenev, Chairman and CEO;"),
    "Shiv Verma": ("8k_jun", "Mr. Verma continues to serve as the Company's CFO and principal financial officer."),
    "Steve Quirk": ("proxy", "Steven Quirk has been our Chief Brokerage Officer since January 2022."),
    "Dan Gallagher": ("proxy", "Daniel Gallagher has been our Chief Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Affairs Officer since January 2022"),
}


def row(name, title, unit, source, quote, status="current", **extra):
    # A unit-scoped office is not the company-wide single-holder role.
    role = None if unit else canonical_role(title, "Robinhood")
    r = {"name": name, "title": title, "level": level(title), "role": role, "unit": unit, "status": status,
         "source": source, "quote": quote, "verified": False}
    if name in ALSO:
        r["also_written"] = ALSO[name]
    if name in SEC_QUOTES and source == LP:
        r["also_supported_by"] = {"source": SEC_QUOTES[name][0], "quote": SEC_QUOTES[name][1]}
    r.update(extra)
    return r


leaders = [row(n, t, u, LP, f"{n} / {t}") for n, t, u in PAGE]
leaders += [
    row("Vlad Tenev", "President", None, "10k", "Chief Executive Officer, President, and Director",
        note="A second office of the same person. Not on the leadership page; from the annual report's signature page."),
    row("Dara Bazzano", "Chief Accounting Officer", None, "8k_jun",
        "Ms. Bazzano, age 58, has been the Company's Chief Accounting Officer since April 2026",
        note="Not listed on the leadership page as accessed on 2026-11-13. Kept on the strength of the SEC filing; please confirm."),
    row("Jason Warnick", "Chief Financial Officer", None, "proxy",
        "Mr. Warnick ceased to serve as Chief Financial Officer effective February 6, 2026", status="former",
        ended="2026-02-06"),
    row("Jeffrey Pinner", "Chief Technology Officer", None, "8k_may",
        "Jeffrey Pinner, Chief Technology Officer, would be separating from his position, effective the same day",
        status="former", ended="2026-05-07", also_written=["Jeff Pinner"]),
]
robinhood = {
    "company": "Robinhood", "domain": "robinhood.com", "as_of": "2026-11-13",
    "drafted_by": "Claude, 2026-11-13; revised 2026-11-13 on the project owner's corrections",
    "verified_by": None, "disclosure": DISCLOSURE,
    "level_convention": "Levels follow the project's rule (SPEC 3.4): any 'Chief ... Officer' or its abbreviation is "
                        "c_level, as is a President who is not a Vice President; otherwise a title with 'Vice "
                        "President' is vp; 'Head of' is head; everything else is other and outside the scope. "
                        "'unit' names the subsidiary or business unit when the title is scoped to one.",
    "sources": {
        LP: {"url": "https://investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership", "accessed": "2026-11-13",
             "how": "Opened in a web browser at the project owner's direction. The pipeline's own fetcher is "
                    "refused by this site and has never read this page; the pipeline's output cannot depend on it."},
        "proxy": {"url": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387926000053/hood-20260422.htm",
                  "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-04-22"},
        "8k_feb": {"url": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387926000013/hood-20260206.htm",
                   "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-02-10"},
        "8k_may": {"url": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387926000065/hood-20260507.htm",
                   "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-05-08"},
        "8k_jun": {"url": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387926000083/hood-20260625.htm",
                   "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-06-26"},
        "10k": {"url": "https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783879/000178387926000023/hood-20251231.htm",
                "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-02-18"},
    },
    "leaders": leaders,
    "unknown": [
        {"item": "Chief Technology Officer", "why": "No source names a successor to Jeffrey Pinner; the leadership "
         "page lists no CTO. Kept unknown until verified."},
        {"item": "Gretchen Howard (COO), Christina Smedley (CMO), Aparna Chennapragada (CPO), Baiju Bhatt (Co-CEO), "
                 "Norm Ashkenas and Kelly Zigaitis (unit Chief Compliance Officers)",

                "accessed on 2026-11-13, but absence from a page is not a statement that someone left. Their "
                "status is not guessed and they are in neither the current nor the former list."},
    ],
}
campfire = {
    "company": "Campfire", "domain": "meetcampfire.com", "as_of": "2026-11-13",
    "drafted_by": "Claude, 2026-11-13; revised 2026-11-13 on the project owner's corrections",

    "level_convention": robinhood["level_convention"],
    "sources": {

                     "how": "The company's own conference page, as fetched by the pipeline and read from its cache."},
        "blog_forecast": {"url": "https://campfire.ai/blog/campfire-announces-forecast-an-end-to-the-mid-month-guessing-game",
                          "accessed": "2026-11-13", "published": "2026-09-18"},
        "blog_claude": {"url": "https://campfire.ai/blog/campfire-accelerates-accounting-with-claude",

"""Finalize the gold sets: coverage groups, company or unit scope, and the owner's approval."""
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])
out = root / "fixtures" / "gold"
APPROVAL = ("The project owner reviewed the rows and their source evidence in chat on 2026-11-13 and approved them. "
            "The owner supplied the list of names on Robinhood's leadership page; the titles were read from the page.")
for name in ("robinhood.com.json", "meetcampfire.com.json"):
    data = json.loads((out / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for r in data["leaders"]:
        title = r["title"].lower()
        groups = [r["level"]] if r["level"] != "other" else []
        # A title that names a vice presidency keeps its level under the project's rule,
        # and also counts toward VP coverage.
        if re.search(r"\bvice president\b", title) and "vp" not in groups:
            groups.append("vp")
        r["counts_toward"] = groups
        r["scope"] = "subsidiary_or_unit" if r.get("unit") else "company"
        r["verified"] = True
    data["verified_by"] = "the project owner, 2026-11-13"
    data["approval"] = APPROVAL
    data["decisions"] = [
        "Titles are kept exactly as the source writes them, and levels follow the project's existing rule.",
        "A person whose title has both 'Vice President' and 'Chief ... Officer' is c_level by that rule and also "
        "counts toward VP coverage ('counts_toward').",
        "Company-level and subsidiary- or unit-level roles are kept separate ('scope', 'unit'). A unit-level "
        "office is never the company-wide single-holder role.",
        "If recall falls below the target, the actual result is reported. The gold set is not changed to pass.",
    ]
    if name.startswith("robinhood"):
        data["decisions"] += [
            "Dara Bazzano is kept as current on the SEC filing of June 2026, although she is not on the leadership page.",
            "Vlad Tenev is also President.",
            "The current CTO and the six officers known only from 2019 to 2021 press releases stay unknown unless "
            "stronger evidence is found.",
        ]
        data["access_note"] = ("Robinhood's leadership page was accessible manually in a web browser on 2026-11-13, "
                               "but it is blocked to this project's fetcher: the site answers 403 to it, including "
                               "for robots.txt. The pipeline therefore cannot use the page that most of this gold "
                               "set comes from, and low recall for Robinhood is expected for that reason.")
    else:
        data["decisions"] += [
            "Chris McDonough is a secondary-source candidate, kept apart from the strict primary-source gold set.",
            "Paul Nichols's current CTO status stays unknown.",
            "John Glasgow is not included as a verified current CFO without stronger evidence.",
        ]
    (out / name).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    rows = data["leaders"]
    cur = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "current"]
    print(f"\n{data['company']}: {len(rows)} rows, all verified: {all(r['verified'] for r in rows)}")
    print("  current rows:", len(cur), "| former rows:", len(rows) - len(cur),
          "| distinct current people:", len({r['name'] for r in cur}))
    for g in ("c_level", "vp", "head"):
        people = sorted({r["name"] for r in cur if g in r["counts_toward"]})
        print(f"  counts toward {g:<8}{len(people):>3} people")
    print("  by scope:", dict(Counter(r["scope"] for r in cur)))
    both = [r["name"] for r in cur if set(r["counts_toward"]) >= {"c_level", "vp"}]
    print("  counted in both C-level and VP:", both)
    print("  outside the scope:", [r["name"] for r in cur if not r["counts_toward"]])
    print("  company-wide single-holder roles:", sorted({r["role"] for r in cur if r["role"]}))

"""Write the fixtures: one JSON file per company and a database holding only those companies. SPEC 3.9.

The JSON is for people and for diffing; the database is what the chat reads.
Every role carries the claims behind it, each with its source and quote.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from .db import claim_key, connect


def _rows(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, args: tuple = ()) -> list[dict]:
    return [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(sql, args).fetchall()]


def company_document(conn: sqlite3.Connection, domain: str) -> dict:
    """Everything stored about one company, as plain data in a stable order."""
    company = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM companies WHERE domain = ?", (domain,)).fetchone()
    if company is None:
        raise KeyError(domain)
    cid = company["id"]
    run = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM runs WHERE company_id = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1", (cid,)).fetchone()
    people = []
    for p in _rows(conn, "SELECT * FROM people WHERE company_id = ? ORDER BY full_name, id", (cid,)):
        claims = _rows(conn, """SELECT cl.*, s.url, s.tier, s.source_type FROM claims cl
                                JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id WHERE cl.person_id = ?
                                ORDER BY s.tier, cl.as_of_date DESC, cl.id""", (p["id"],))
        roles = []
        for r in _rows(conn, """SELECT * FROM roles WHERE person_id = ? ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'current' THEN 0
                                WHEN 'announced' THEN 1 WHEN 'unverified' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, title""", (p["id"],)):
            key = r["canonical_role"] or claim_key(r["title"], r["level"], r["department"], None)
            roles.append({
                "title": r["title"], "level": r["level"], "department": r["department"],
                "canonical_role": r["canonical_role"], "status": r["status"], "decided_by": r["status_reason"],
                "starts_on": r["starts_on"], "ended_on": r["ended_on"], "end_reported_on": r["end_reported_on"],
                "first_seen": r["first_seen"], "last_seen": r["last_seen"],
                "last_verified_at": r["last_verified_at"], "conflict": bool(r["conflict"]),
                "conflict_reason": r["conflict_reason"], "source_count": r["source_count"],
                "claims": [{
                    "type": c["claim_type"], "scope": c["departure_scope"], "title": c["raw_title"],
                    "name_as_written": c["person_as_written"], "evidence": c["evidence"],
                    "effective_date": c["effective_date"], "pending": bool(c["effective_pending"]),
                    "as_of_date": c["as_of_date"], "as_of_basis": c["as_of_basis"], "source_url": c["url"],
                    "tier": c["tier"], "source_type": c["source_type"]}
                    for c in claims if c["claim_type"] in ("role", "appointment", "departure")
                    and claim_key(c["raw_title"], c["level"], c["department"], c["canonical_role"]) == key]})

        def fact(kind: str) -> dict | None:
            c = next((c for c in claims if c["claim_type"] == kind), None)
            check = conn.execute("SELECT outcome FROM checks WHERE person_id = ? AND kind = ? ORDER BY id DESC "
                                 "LIMIT 1", (p["id"], kind)).fetchone()
            if c:
                return {"value": c["value"], "status": "found", "evidence": c["evidence"], "source_url": c["url"]}
            return {"value": None, "status": check["outcome"], "evidence": None, "source_url": None} if check else None

        other = conn.execute("SELECT full_name FROM people WHERE id = ?", (p["possible_duplicate_of"],)).fetchone() \
            if p["possible_duplicate_of"] else None
        people.append({"name": p["full_name"], "employment_status": p["employment_status"],
                       "may_be_the_same_person_as": other["full_name"] if other else None,
                       "location": fact("location"), "bio": fact("bio"), "roles": roles})
    return {
        "company": company["name"], "domain": company["domain"], "collected_at": company["collected_at"],
        "run": {"status": run["status"], "reasons": json.loads(run["reasons"]),
                "counters": json.loads(run["counters"])} if run else None,
        "people": people,
        "sources": _rows(conn, """SELECT url, source_type, tier, title, published_at, retrieved_at, stage, page_kind,
                                  last_error FROM sources WHERE company_id = ? ORDER BY tier, url""", (cid,)),
        "checks": [{**c, "queries": json.loads(c["queries"])} for c in _rows(
            conn, """SELECT p.full_name AS person, k.kind, k.role_key, k.queries, k.outcome, k.detail, k.checked_at
                     FROM checks k LEFT JOIN people p ON p.id = k.person_id WHERE k.company_id = ?
                     ORDER BY k.kind, p.full_name, k.id""", (cid,))],
    }


def export(source_db: Path, out_dir: Path, domains: list[str]) -> list[Path]:
    """Write <domain>.json for each company and leadership.db with only those companies."""
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    conn = connect(source_db)
    written: list[Path] = []
    for domain in domains:
        path = out_dir / f"{domain}.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(company_document(conn, domain), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
                        encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written.append(path)
    conn.close()

    target = out_dir / "leadership.db"
    target.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    src = sqlite3.connect(source_db)
    dst = sqlite3.connect(target)
    src.backup(dst)
    src.close()
    marks = ",".join("?" * len(domains))
    keep = f"(SELECT id FROM companies WHERE domain IN ({marks}))"
    dst.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF")
    for table in ("roles", "checks", "claims", "people", "sources", "runs"):
        dst.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE company_id NOT IN {keep}", domains)
    dst.execute(f"DELETE FROM companies WHERE domain NOT IN ({marks})", domains)
    dst.commit()
    dst.execute("VACUUM")
    dst.close()
    written.append(target)
    return written

def conn(tmp_path):
    c = connect(tmp_path / "t.db")
    c.execute("INSERT INTO companies (id, domain, name) VALUES (1, 'acme-robotics.com', 'Acme Robotics')")
    c.execute("INSERT INTO companies (id, domain, name) VALUES (2, 'other.com', 'Other')")
    c.execute("INSERT INTO sources (id, company_id, url, source_type, tier, published_at, retrieved_at, stage) "

def _person(conn, pid, name, source, kind, title, canonical, level, **kw):
    conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO people (id, company_id, full_name, normalized_name) VALUES (?,1,?,?)",
                 (pid, name, name.lower()))
    conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO claims (company_id, person_id, source_id, claim_type, departure_scope, raw_title, level,
               department, canonical_role, value, evidence, as_of_date, as_of_basis, extraction_version,
               person_as_written)
           VALUES (1,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,'published','v1',?)""",

    _person(conn, 1, "Vladimir Tenev", 1, "role", "Chair and Chief Executive Officer", "CEO", "c_level")
    _person(conn, 2, "Evan McHenry", 1, "role", "Chief Information Security Officer", "CISO", "c_level")

    _person(conn, 4, "Jason Warnick", 1, "role", "Chief Financial Officer", "CFO", "c_level")              # gold: former

    assert (c_level["gold"], c_level["current"]) == (3, 2)             # Tenev by nickname, McHenry; not Koller
    assert c_level["missing"] == ["Walter Koller"]
    assert (vp["gold"], vp["current"]) == (3, 1)                       # McHenry counts toward VP too

"""Deterministic normalization of titles and names. SPEC sections 3.4 and 3.5.

Pure functions, no I/O and no model, so every rule is unit-testable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

from .sources.edgar import core_name

DEPARTMENTS = ("engineering", "product", "marketing", "sales", "finance", "legal", "people",
               "operations", "design", "data", "security", "other")

# Single-holder roles with a common short form. Any other "Chief X Officer"
# keeps its full wording as the canonical role.
_CHIEFS = {
    "executive": "CEO", "financial": "CFO", "finance": "CFO", "technology": "CTO",
    "technical": "CTO", "operating": "COO", "operations": "COO", "marketing": "CMO",
    "product": "CPO", "legal": "CLO", "information": "CIO", "revenue": "CRO",
    "information security": "CISO", "people": "Chief People Officer",
    "human resources": "CHRO",
}
_ABBREVIATIONS = {"ceo": "CEO", "cfo": "CFO", "cto": "CTO", "coo": "COO", "cmo": "CMO",
                  "cpo": "CPO", "clo": "CLO", "cio": "CIO", "cro": "CRO", "ciso": "CISO",
                  "chro": "CHRO"}
_OFFICE = r"\bofficer\b|\b(?:" + "|".join(_ABBREVIATIONS) + r")\b"
_CHIEF = re.compile(r"\bchief\s+([a-z&,\s]+?)\s+officer\b")
_VP = re.compile(r"\b(?:[se]?vp|vice[\s-]+president)\b")
_HEAD = re.compile(r"\b(?:global\s+)?head\s+of\b|\bhead,\s")
_PRESIDENT = re.compile(r"(?<!vice )(?<!vice-)\bpresident\b")
# Words that follow an office without naming a part of the company.
_OTHER_ROLE = re.compile(r"^(?:co-?\s?founder|founder|chair|president|director|chief|general|"
                         r"secretary|treasurer|member|the\s+board|board|principal)\b")


def _plain(title: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", title.replace("&", " and ").casefold()).strip()


def level(title: str | None) -> str:
    """c_level, vp, head or other, from the title's wording."""
    if not title:
        return "other"
    t = _plain(title)
    if _CHIEF.search(t) or any(re.search(rf"\b{a}\b", t) for a in _ABBREVIATIONS):
        return "c_level"
    if _VP.search(t):
        return "vp"                     # includes "Senior Vice President" and "VP of ..."
    if _PRESIDENT.search(t) or re.search(r"\bgeneral counsel\b", t):
        return "c_level"
    if _HEAD.search(t):
        return "head"
    return "other"                      # directors, board members, founders without an office


def has_division(title: str, company: str | None = None) -> bool:
    """The title names a part of the company: 'CEO of Robinhood Crypto'.

    'CEO of Robinhood Markets, Inc.' names the company itself, not a part.
    """
    after = re.split(_OFFICE, _plain(title))[-1]
    for part in re.split(r",|\band\b|;|/|\(|\)", after):
        named = re.sub(r"^(?:of|at|for)\s+", "", part.strip(" -–—"))
        if not named or _OTHER_ROLE.match(named) or not core_name(named):
            continue
        if company and core_name(named) == core_name(company):
            continue
        return True
    return False


def canonical_role(title: str | None, company: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The single-holder role a title names, or None.

    'President and CEO' -> CEO; 'Chief Compliance Officer' keeps its wording;
    'CEO of Robinhood Crypto' -> None, because it is one division's CEO.

def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Lower case, no accents, no titles, suffixes, middle initials or punctuation."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch)).casefold()
    text = re.sub(r"\([^)]*\)|\"[^\"]*\"", " ", text)           # nicknames in brackets or quotes
    words = [w.strip(".") for w in re.sub(r"[^a-z.'\-\s]", " ", text).split()]
    words = [w for w in words if w and w not in _SUFFIXES and w not in _PREFIXES]
    if len(words) > 2:                                          # drop middle initials
        words = [words[0]] + [w for w in words[1:-1] if len(w) > 1] + [words[-1]]
    return " ".join(words)


def _same_given_name(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    return a == b or any(a in group and b in group for group in _NICKNAMES)


def compare_names(a: str, b: str) -> str:
    """How two normalized names relate: 'same', 'nickname', 'near' or 'different'.

    'nickname' needs a matching role before the two are merged; 'near' is
    never merged, only flagged for a human.
    """
    if a == b:
        return "same"
    wa, wb = a.split(), b.split()
    if len(wa) < 2 or len(wb) < 2 or wa[-1] != wb[-1]:
        return "different"
    if _same_given_name(wa[0], wb[0]):
        # "Vlad Tenev" and "Vladimir Tenev"; or the same first name with an extra middle name.
        return "nickname" if wa[0] != wb[0] else "near"
    if wa[0][0] == wb[0][0] and (len(wa[0]) == 1 or len(wb[0]) == 1):
        return "near"                                           # "J Warnick" and "Jason Warnick"
    return "different"

toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Re-check every stored claim against the saved page it came from. No model, no network.

    uv run python tools/check_evidence.py

For each claim in data/leadership.db: the evidence quote must be in the cached
page, the person's full name must be in it, and the quote must be next to the
name. Also checks that every role marked current has a supporting claim.
Exit code 1 if anything fails.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
from leadership.cache import FileCache  # noqa: E402
from leadership.db import connect  # noqa: E402
from leadership.extract import ExtractedClaim, Target, check_claim  # noqa: E402
from leadership.sources.web import clean_text  # noqa: E402


def main() -> int:
    conn = connect(ROOT / "data" / "leadership.db")
    pages = FileCache(ROOT / "cache" / "pages")
    texts: dict[str, str] = {}
    failures = total = 0
    for company in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM companies ORDER BY id").fetchall():
        target = Target(company["name"], {company["domain"]})
        rows = conn.execute(
            """SELECT cl.*, p.full_name, s.url FROM claims cl JOIN people p ON p.id = cl.person_id
                 JOIN sources s ON s.id = cl.source_id WHERE cl.company_id = ? ORDER BY cl.id""",
            (company["id"],)).fetchall()
        bad = 0
        for r in rows:
            if r["url"] not in texts:
                hit = pages.get(r["url"])
                texts[r["url"]] = clean_text(hit["body"]) if hit and hit.get("body") else ""
            claim = ExtractedClaim(person=r["person_as_written"] or r["full_name"],
                                   organization=company["name"],
                                   claim_type=r["claim_type"], raw_title=r["raw_title"],
                                   value=r["value"], evidence=r["evidence"])
            reason = "the page is not in the cache" if not texts[r["url"]] else \
                check_claim(claim, texts[r["url"]], target)
            if reason:
                bad += 1
                print(f"  FAIL claim {r['id']} ({r['person_as_written']} / {r['raw_title']}): {reason}\n"
                      f"       {r['url'][:100]}")
        orphans = conn.execute(
            """SELECT count(*) FROM roles r WHERE r.company_id = ? AND r.status = 'current'
                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM claims c WHERE c.id = r.supporting_claim_id)""",
            (company["id"],)).fetchone()[0]
        current = conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM roles WHERE company_id = ? AND status = 'current'",
                               (company["id"],)).fetchone()[0]
        versions = conn.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT extraction_version) FROM claims WHERE company_id = ?",
                                (company["id"],)).fetchone()[0]
        print(f"{company['name']:<12}{len(rows):>4} claims re-checked, {bad} failed; {current} current roles, "
              f"{orphans} without a supporting claim; {versions} extraction version(s) in use")
        total += len(rows)
        failures += bad + orphans
    print(f"\n{total} claims checked: {failures} problems")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Deterministic normalization of titles and names. SPEC sections 3.4 and 3.5.

Pure functions, no I/O and no model, so every rule is unit-testable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

from .sources.edgar import core_name

DEPARTMENTS = ("engineering", "product", "marketing", "sales", "finance", "legal", "people",
               "operations", "design", "data", "security", "other")

# Single-holder roles with a common short form. Any other "Chief X Officer"
# keeps its full wording as the canonical role.
_CHIEFS = {
    "executive": "CEO", "financial": "CFO", "finance": "CFO", "technology": "CTO",
    "technical": "CTO", "operating": "COO", "operations": "COO", "marketing": "CMO",
    "product": "CPO", "legal": "CLO", "information": "CIO", "revenue": "CRO",
    "information security": "CISO", "people": "Chief People Officer",
    "human resources": "CHRO",
}
_ABBREVIATIONS = {"ceo": "CEO", "cfo": "CFO", "cto": "CTO", "coo": "COO", "cmo": "CMO",
                  "cpo": "CPO", "clo": "CLO", "cio": "CIO", "cro": "CRO", "ciso": "CISO",
                  "chro": "CHRO"}
_OFFICE = r"\bofficer\b|\b(?:" + "|".join(_ABBREVIATIONS) + r")\b"
# "finance chief and principal financial officer" is not a "Chief ... Officer" title.
_CHIEF = re.compile(r"\bchief\s+(?!and\b)([a-z&,\s]+?)\s+officer\b")
_VP = re.compile(r"\b(?:[se]?vp|vice[\s-]+president)\b")
_HEAD = re.compile(r"\b(?:global\s+)?head\s+of\b|\bhead,\s")
_PRESIDENT = re.compile(r"(?<!vice )(?<!vice-)\bpresident\b")
# Words that follow an office without naming a part of the company.
_OTHER_ROLE = re.compile(r"^(?:co-?\s?founder|founder|chair|president|director|chief|general|"
                         r"secretary|treasurer|member|the\s+board|board|principal)\b")


def _plain(title: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", title.replace("&", " and ").casefold()).strip()


def level(title: str | None) -> str:
    """c_level, vp, head or other, from the title's wording."""
    if not title:
        return "other"
    t = _plain(title)
    if _CHIEF.search(t) or any(re.search(rf"\b{a}\b", t) for a in _ABBREVIATIONS):
        return "c_level"
    if _VP.search(t):
        return "vp"                     # includes "Senior Vice President" and "VP of ..."
    if _PRESIDENT.search(t) or re.search(r"\bgeneral counsel\b", t):
        return "c_level"
    if _HEAD.search(t):
        return "head"
    return "other"                      # directors, board members, founders without an office


def has_division(title: str, company: str | None = None) -> bool:
    """The title names a part of the company: 'CEO of Robinhood Crypto'.

    'CEO of Robinhood Markets, Inc.' names the company itself, not a part.
    """
    after = re.split(_OFFICE, _plain(title))[-1]
    for part in re.split(r",|\band\b|;|/|\(|\)", after):
        named = re.sub(r"^(?:of|at|for)\s+", "", part.strip(" -–—"))
        if not named or _OTHER_ROLE.match(named) or not core_name(named):
            continue
        if company and core_name(named) == core_name(company):
            continue
        return True
    return False


def canonical_role(title: str | None, company: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The single-holder role a title names, or None.

    'President and CEO' -> CEO; 'Chief Compliance Officer' keeps its wording;
    'CEO of Robinhood Crypto' -> None, because it is one division's CEO.
    When a title names two offices the first is used; extraction is asked to
    give one claim per office.
    """
    if not title:
        return None
    t = _plain(title)
    found: str | None = None
    if m := _CHIEF.search(t):
        # Commas and "and" are spelled differently by different sources.
        what = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", m.group(1).replace(",", " ")).strip()
        named = " ".join(w if w == "and" else w.capitalize() for w in what.split())
        found = _CHIEFS.get(what) or f"Chief {named} Officer"
    else:
        first = min(((m.start(), role) for a, role in _ABBREVIATIONS.items()
                     if (m := re.search(rf"\b{a}\b", t))), default=None)
        found = first[1] if first else None
    if found and has_division(title, company):
        return None
    return found


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- names
_SUFFIXES = {"jr", "sr", "ii", "iii", "iv", "phd", "md", "mba", "cpa", "esq", "cfa", "jd"}
_PREFIXES = {"dr", "mr", "mrs", "ms", "prof", "sir"}
_NICKNAMES = [
    {"vlad", "vladimir"}, {"bill", "will", "william"}, {"bob", "rob", "robert"},
    {"mike", "michael"}, {"dan", "daniel"}, {"jim", "james"}, {"tom", "thomas"},
    {"chris", "christopher"}, {"matt", "matthew"}, {"steve", "steven", "stephen"},
    {"dave", "david"}, {"joe", "joseph"}, {"ben", "benjamin"}, {"alex", "alexander"},
    {"kate", "katherine", "catherine", "kathy", "cathy"}, {"liz", "beth", "elizabeth"},
    {"jeff", "jeffrey"}, {"greg", "gregory"}, {"tony", "anthony"}, {"nick", "nicholas"},
    {"sam", "samuel", "samantha"}, {"andy", "andrew"}, {"jon", "jonathan"},
    {"tim", "timothy"}, {"pat", "patrick", "patricia"}, {"rick", "rich", "richard"},
    {"ed", "edward"}, {"ken", "kenneth"}, {"ron", "ronald"}, {"sue", "susan"},
]


def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Lower case, no accents, no titles, suffixes, middle initials or punctuation."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch)).casefold()
    text = re.sub(r"\([^)]*\)|\"[^\"]*\"", " ", text)           # nicknames in brackets or quotes
    words = [w.strip(".") for w in re.sub(r"[^a-z.'\-\s]", " ", text).split()]
    words = [w for w in words if w and w not in _SUFFIXES and w not in _PREFIXES]
    if len(words) > 2:                                          # drop middle initials
        words = [words[0]] + [w for w in words[1:-1] if len(w) > 1] + [words[-1]]
    return " ".join(words)


def _same_given_name(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    return a == b or any(a in group and b in group for group in _NICKNAMES)


def compare_names(a: str, b: str) -> str:
    """How two normalized names relate: 'same', 'nickname', 'near' or 'different'.

    'nickname' needs a matching role before the two are merged; 'near' is
    never merged, only flagged for a human.
    """
    if a == b:
        return "same"
    wa, wb = a.split(), b.split()
    if len(wa) < 2 or len(wb) < 2 or wa[-1] != wb[-1]:
        return "different"
    if _same_given_name(wa[0], wb[0]):
        # "Vlad Tenev" and "Vladimir Tenev"; or the same first name with an extra middle name.
        return "nickname" if wa[0] != wb[0] else "near"
    if wa[0][0] == wb[0][0] and (len(wa[0]) == 1 or len(wb[0]) == 1):
        return "near"                                           # "J Warnick" and "Jason Warnick"
    return "different"

"""One-off patch (M4): SPEC and README."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(sys.argv[1])


def patch(path, pairs):
    p = root / path
    s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for old, new in pairs:
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (path, old[:60], s.count(old))
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


patch("SPEC.md", [

# M4 acceptance report: verify, enrich, export, gold sets, held-out company

- **Run date:** 2026-11-13
- **Branch:** `m4-verify` (log captured before the M4 commit, on top of `3c20f6b`)
- **Raw evidence:** [M4_results.log](M4_results.log) — full, unedited command output.
  Also [M4_heldout_wise_first_run.log](M4_heldout_wise_first_run.log) and
  [M4_no_data_run.log](M4_no_data_run.log), the first runs of the held-out
  company and of the no-data input.
- **Reproduce:** `uv run python tools/acceptance.py M4`
- **Needs:** an LLM key and the search key. See "Real calls and cached
  answers" below for what the recorded run actually called.

## 1. Automated results

All numbers below are copied from `M4_results.log`.

| # | Step | Expected | Actual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M4 tests | all pass | 20 passed | PASS |
| 2 | Whole fast suite | all pass | 318 passed, 13 deselected (the 13 need keys) | PASS |
| 3 | Real-model tests | all pass | 6 passed | PASS |
| 4 | Campfire, full run | `complete` | `complete`; 16 claims about 5 people; 3 current leaders, 1 unverified | PASS |
| 5 | Robinhood, full run | `complete` | `complete`; 144 claims about 27 people; 5 current leaders, 7 unverified people | PASS |
| 6 | Export | files written | `fixtures/meetcampfire.com.json`, `fixtures/robinhood.com.json`, `fixtures/leadership.db` | PASS |
| 7 | Measurement | reported | Labelled pages: precision 100%, recall 100%. Gold sets: see section 2 | PASS (measured; one target not met) |
| 8 | Every stored claim re-checked | 0 problems | 168 claims, 0 problems; every current role has a supporting claim | PASS |
| 9, 10 | Leaders with evidence, location, biography | listing | both printed | PASS |
| 11, 12 | Every targeted check and its outcome | listing | 7 for Campfire, 25 for Robinhood | PASS |
| 13, 14 | Held-out company (Wise) | listing | 1 current leader, 4 people | PASS |
| 15 | No-data input | `insufficient_data`, exit code 3 | `insufficient_data` with three reasons, no error | PASS |
| 16 | M1 mutation check | all caught | 23 of 23 | PASS |
| 17 | Secret scan | 0 problems | 186 files scanned (110 of them run logs), 0 problems | PASS |

17 of 17 steps ran as expected. **A step passing means it ran and reported;
it does not mean every target was met.** The C-level recall target is not met
for Robinhood (section 2).

### Real calls and cached answers

| Part | In the recorded acceptance run | Where the stored results came from |
|---|---|---|
| Fast tests | no call | no model, or a recorded answer placed in the cache by the test |
| Real-model tests (step 3) | **real model calls** | fresh each time |
| Campfire (step 4) | 0 searches, 0 model calls | the verification run at 11:25 UTC the same day: 5 searches, 16 model calls |
| Robinhood (step 5) | **2 searches, 7 model calls** (one newly surfaced role was checked) | mostly two earlier runs the same day: 18 searches and 68 model calls, then 10 searches and 16 model calls |
| Labelled pages (step 7) | 0 model calls | calls made earlier the same day with the same prompt |
| Gold-set measurement | no call | reads `fixtures/leadership.db` |
| Wise and the no-data input | 0 calls (already run) | their first runs: Wise 8 searches and 28 model calls; no-data 7 searches and 3 model calls |

In total M4 used about 50 search queries on 2026-11-13.

## 2. Measurement against the gold sets

The gold sets are in `fixtures/gold/`. They were drafted by Claude from
primary sources and approved row by row by the project owner on 2026-11-13.
**They are not fully blind to earlier pipeline results**; each file says so.
Recall is measured against the gold sets only.

| | Campfire | Robinhood |
|---|---|---|
| C-level people in the gold set | 1 | 11 |
| ... found as current | 1 (100%) | 5 (45%) |
| VP people in the gold set | 0 | 14 |
| ... found as current | n/a | **0 (0%)** |
| Head people in the gold set | 2 | 0 |
| ... found as current | 1 (50%) | n/a |
| Roles the pipeline marks current | 3 | 7 (5 people) |
| ... correct by the gold set | 2 | 6 |
| ... wrong by the gold set | 0 | 0 |
| ... not judged or not counted | 1 (Chris McDonough, secondary candidate) | 1 (Daniel Gallagher, "Chief Legal Officer") |
| Precision of current roles | 100% (provisional) | 100% (provisional) |
| Gold-set former leaders reported as current | 0 | 0 |

| Target (SPEC 7.4) | Campfire | Robinhood |
|---|---|---|
| Precision of current roles at least 90% | met, provisional | met, provisional |
| C-level recall 100% | met | **NOT MET: 45%** |
| No former leader reported as current | met | met |

"Provisional" because one role per company is not judged by the gold set.
You can judge them in `fixtures/gold/<domain>_review.json` (manual test
MT-4.4).

### VP and Head coverage (R161)

- **Robinhood: none of the 14 vice presidents was found.** This is a gap, not
  a pass. Not found: Pooja Anand, Robb Baldwin, Matt Billings, Abhishek
  Fatehpuria, Johann Kerbrat, Chris Koegel, Walter Koller, Seok Lee, JB
  Mackenzie, Evan McHenry, Ravi Mehta, Lucas Moskowitz, Deepak Rao, Nicola
  White.
- **Robinhood C-level not found (6):** Stephanie Guild, Connie Schan, Evan
  McHenry, Walter Koller, Ravi Mehta, Jordan Sinclair.
- **Campfire: 1 of 2 heads found.** Brendan Doyle (Head of Product) is named
  only in a blog post's author line, which the model did not return.

**Why Robinhood's recall is low.** All of the missing people are named on
`investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership`. That page was accessible
manually in a browser on 2026-11-13 but is blocked to this project's
fetcher: the site answers 403 to it. The pipeline's Robinhood sources are SEC
filings, which name only the executive officers, and press releases. The
gold set was not changed to make the target pass.

## 3. What the new stages did

**Carried from M3**

| Requirement | Result |
|---|---|
| R160 leaders named only as a speaker, host or author | Labelled pages: recall 100% (was 82%). Both CEO pairs missed in M3 are found |
| R164 stated dates recovered | Jason Warnick's CFO role now ends on 2026-02-06, with the proxy sentence as evidence. In the final data the model returned that sentence itself; the model-free recovery is covered by `test_a_date_the_model_missed_is_recovered_from_a_held_source` |
| R165 first-party pages not refused on the model's judgment | Regression test; the override fired on real Robinhood pages |

**Former roles that still have no end date** (R164 asks for this list):

| Person | Role | Does a held source state a date? |
|---|---|---|
| Shiv Verma | Senior Vice President of Finance and Strategy, and Treasurer | No. "had been our ... since 2018" gives no end date |
| Anne Hoge | Chief Legal Officer | No. "leaving Robinhood later this month" gives no day |

**Verification (3.7).** 13 checks on Robinhood roles and 1 on Campfire, each
with up to two model-proposed queries and at most three new pages.

| Outcome | Campfire | Robinhood |
|---|---|---|
| still unverified | 1 | 8 |
| conflict remains | 0 | 4 |
| role no longer present | 0 | 1 |
| confirmed current | 0 | 0 |
| ended | 0 | 0 |

**No check ended in a confirmed or ended role.** Searches found third-party
pages, and the rules do not let those settle an office. Four roles now carry
a conflict flag, "departure reported by news only; no company source
confirms it": Baiju Bhatt, Christina Smedley and Norm Ashkenas. They stay
`unverified`, as you asked for the six historical officers.

**Enrichment (3.8).** Looked up for the 3 current Campfire leaders and the 5
current Robinhood leaders.

| | Campfire | Robinhood |
|---|---|---|
| Location found | 0 of 3 | 0 of 5 |
| Location recorded as "not found" | 3 | 5 |
| Biography found | 2 of 3 | 5 of 5 |

No personal location was found for anyone, including both CEOs. Each has an
explicit "not found". The check that refuses a company address as a person's
location is tested but never fired on real data.

**Held-out company: Wise** (chosen by you; run once before any change).

- First run: `complete`; 24 pages, 8 searches, 28 model calls. The second
  search round ran because no CEO had been found, and then found one.
- Found: Kristo Käärmann, co-founder and CEO, current. Also stored, outside
  the scope: David Wells (chair), Scott Hill (non-executive director),
  Taavet Hinrikus (co-founder).
- **Hand-check of everything it stored (4 people, 5 roles): all correct**,
  checked against the article quotes and Wise's own leadership page.
- **Coverage: 1 of 9.** Wise's leadership page lists nine leaders (CEO, CFO,
  CTO, CPO, Chief Banking & Expansion Officer, Head of Global Operations,
  Chief People Officer, Chief Legal Officer, Group Chief Compliance
  Officer). Like Robinhood's, `owners.wise.com` refuses the fetcher; I read
  it in a browser for this hand-check only.
- **One general bug found and fixed:** "co-founder and chief executive"
  (British usage, no "officer") was not read as CEO. No company-specific code
  was added. All three companies were then run again.

**No-data input:** `example.com` ended `insufficient_data` with three
reasons and no error.

## 4. Checklist rows covered

| Row | Requirement (short) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R15 | Shared roles stay current after verification | M1 worked cases 40 to 45; verification only adds claims, so the same rule applies |
| R35 | A targeted check for every unverified or conflicting role | Steps 11, 12; `test_each_uncertain_role_gets_one_check_and_the_rules_decide` |
| R36 | Gold set per company | `fixtures/gold/`; **not written before pipeline output was seen**, disclosed in each file |
| R37 | Precision of current roles at least 90% | Step 7: 100% for both, provisional |
| R38 | All gold C-level people found | **Not met for Robinhood: 5 of 11.** Met for Campfire |
| R39 | No gold former leader reported as current | Step 7: 0 for both |
| R40 | Every current role traces to a source and a checked quote | Step 8 |
| R41 | Location as a sourced claim, or recorded as not found | 8 of 8 recorded as not found; `test_enrichment_stores_...` |
| R42 | Headquarters never used as a person's location | `test_location_checks_refuse_a_company_address_...` |
| R43 | Short biography | 7 of 8; quality varies (section 6) |
| R44 | JSON export per company | Step 6; `test_export_...` |
| R103 | Queries proposed by the model, statuses set by rules | Step 12 lists the queries; `verify.py` never writes a status |
| R104 | A supported claim is not thereby believed | The seven unverified Robinhood officers |
| R105 | Precision by hand-judging current roles | `fixtures/gold/*_review.json`; two rows await your verdict |
| R106 | Held-out company | Section 3; `M4_heldout_wise_first_run.log` |
| R107 | No-data input ends `insufficient_data` | Step 15; `M4_no_data_run.log` |
| R108 | Source count per role | `source_count` in the `leadership` view and the export |
| R160, R164, R165 | Carried from M3 | Section 3 |
| R161 | VP and Head coverage checked explicitly | Section 2 |
| R166, R167 | New in M4 (section 5) | Their own tests |

## 5. Errors and issues met during M4

| # | What happened | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **An investor was stored as a Campfire CEO.** After the prompt change the model returned John Locke of Accel as CEO, with a genuine quote from the Series A post | The checks only asked that the quote be in the page and near his name. The quote never says he holds the office; another person's title stood in it | New requirement R166: the title must be in the same sentence as the person's name, or the quote must refer to them by pronoun. He is refused. Six regression tests |
| 2 | That rule first refused correct claims: "Dr. Naomi Boyd has joined Robinhood Markets, Inc. as ..." and "Since joining as Vice President of Operations, Gretchen's leadership ..." | Sentences were cut at "Dr." and "Inc."; and a given name alone was not accepted | Abbreviations no longer end a sentence; a given name ties a title unless it is followed by a different surname |
| 3 | Shiv Verma's earlier post showed as current again | The model returned "had been our Senior Vice President" as a plain role this time | New requirement R167: when the company's own later document calls a title an earlier one, it is no longer current. No model involved |
| 4 | My new tests failed before any real run | Sentences were cut at "Mr."; a log field name clashed with a parameter | Fixed; this is why the stage tests were written first |
| 5 | A role unrelated to an office carried that office's name | A company-wide departure lent its office to the person's other roles (an M1 rule) | Fixed in the rules; test added; mutation check still 23 of 23 |
| 6 | "finance chief and principal financial officer" was read as a "Chief ... Officer" title | The pattern allowed "and" straight after "chief" | Fixed; test added |
| 7 | Re-processing a page would have dropped a stored biography for good | The lookup was skipped whenever an earlier result existed | A found fact whose claim is gone is looked up again, from the cached answer |
| 8 | The evidence re-check reported 2 failures | It applied role checks to biographies | Biography and location claims are re-checked with their own rules: 168 of 168 pass |
| 9 | **A second Robinhood run spent 10 more searches I did not expect** | Pages found for one person named other people, who became new uncertain roles and were checked on the next run | Bounded per run (15 checks) but not across runs. Documented in the spec and README; not changed |
| 10 | Campfire's verification run ended `partial_failure` | One third-party site answered HTTP 429 (rate limit) | Handled as designed; the next run was `complete` |
| 11 | "chief executive" was not read as CEO (Wise) | British usage without "officer" | Fixed as a general rule; test added |

Issue 1 matters most. It is the same class of fault you found in M3: a
plausible claim with a real quote that does not actually support it.

## 6. Limitations

- **Coverage is set by what a site lets the tool read.** For Robinhood and
  Wise the official leadership page is closed to the fetcher. The pipeline
  does not find vice presidents or most chief officers there.
- **Verification by search did not settle any role.** It adds third-party
  evidence, which the rules rightly treat as weak.
- **Repeated runs can keep spending searches** (issue 9).
- **No personal location was found.** Leaders' locations are rarely stated
  in the sources read.
- **Biographies are thin.** Each is one or two quoted sentences. Some only
  restate the title, such as "Kristo Käärmann is the co-founder and CEO of
  Wise."
- **The gold sets are not fully blind**, and precision is provisional until
  the two unjudged roles are judged.
- **Two former roles have no end date**, because no source states one.
- **The model is not fully repeatable.** Results moved between runs: the
  Warnick sentence was returned in one run and not in another. The
  model-free recovery and the checks are what keep the stored data stable.
- **Brendan Doyle is missed.** An author line under a blog post is not
  extracted as a leader.

## 7. Decisions made during M4 that the spec did not fix

Please confirm or change these in manual test MT-4.8.

1. **Verification and enrichment are part of `leadership collect`**;
   `--no-verify` stops before them.
2. **A check reads at most three new pages.**
3. **A role is checked once.** It is not searched again on later runs.
4. **Stated dates and earlier titles are recovered without a model**, by
   strict sentence rules. Sentences that disagree add nothing.
5. **The title must be tied to the person** (R166), replacing the
   250-character rule for titles. The window still applies to dates and to
   "is the quote about this person at all".
6. **A biography is quoted text**, never a summary written by the model.
7. **The location search is one query per person**, made only when the held
   sources give no location.
8. **`leadership eval` measures the fixtures**, not the working database,
   when fixtures exist. `export` must be run first.
9. **Precision counts only judged roles.** Unjudged and secondary-candidate
   roles are shown and counted apart, never as correct.
10. **A gold row counts toward every group its title names**, and unit-level
    offices never match a company-wide office (your instruction).
11. **A new `checks` table** and a `location_status` column in the view.
12. **Wise's leadership page was read in a browser for the hand-check
    only**, as you did for Robinhood. The pipeline did not read it.

## 8. Manual acceptance tests

Run these in a terminal opened in the project folder (PowerShell). MT-4.1 to
MT-4.3 and MT-4.5 make no outside call.

- [ ] **MT-4.1 Fast tests.** Run `uv run pytest`.
  Expected: last line reads `318 passed, 13 deselected`.

- [ ] **MT-4.2 Measurement.** Run `uv run leadership eval --gold-only`.
  Expected: the tables of section 2: Robinhood C-level 5 of 11, VP 0 of 14,
  "Target C-level recall = 100%: NOT MET"; Campfire C-level 1 of 1, Head 1
  of 2.

- [ ] **MT-4.3 Evidence.** Run `uv run python tools/check_evidence.py`.
  Expected: `168 claims checked: 0 problems`.

- [ ] **MT-4.4 Judge the two open roles.** Open
  `fixtures/gold/robinhood.com_review.json` and
  `fixtures/gold/meetcampfire.com_review.json`. For "Daniel Gallagher | Chief
  Legal Officer", set `hand_verdict` to `correct` or `wrong`. Decide whether
  Chris McDonough stays "not counted". Run MT-4.2 again.
  Expected: precision is no longer marked provisional for Robinhood.

- [ ] **MT-4.5 Verification record.** Run
  `uv run python tools/show_people.py robinhood.com --checks`.
  Expected: 25 checks; each verification lists its queries and an outcome;
  none says "confirmed_current" or "ended". Check that the queries are
  sensible.

- [ ] **MT-4.6 Leaders, with location and biography.** Run
  `uv run python tools/show_people.py robinhood.com`.
  Expected: each current leader shows "location: not found" and a quoted
  biography; Jason Warnick is former, "ended on 2026-02-06". Decide whether
  any biography is unacceptable.

- [ ] **MT-4.7 The fixtures.** Open `fixtures/robinhood.com.json`.
  Expected: for a current role, its claims with source URL and quote. Compare
  one with the source.

- [ ] **MT-4.8 Decisions.** Read section 7 and confirm or change each of the
  twelve decisions.

- [ ] **MT-4.9 Held-out company.** Run `uv run python tools/show_people.py wise.com --all`
  and compare with my hand-check in section 3.

- [ ] **MT-4.10 Checklist.** In `SPEC_checklist.xlsx`, filter Milestone to
  `M4` and review the Status and Notes.

## 9. Open questions for you

1. **C-level recall is 45% for Robinhood against a target of 100%.** The
   cause is access, not a bug I can fix without imitating a browser. Options:
   accept and document it; or let a user supply a saved copy of a leadership
   page as an extra source; or lower the target. I recommend the first for
   this milestone and noting the second as a possible feature.
2. **Daniel Gallagher as "Chief Legal Officer"** (MT-4.4): the proxy says
   "our Chief Legal Officer since May 2020" as well as his current longer
   title. Correct or wrong?
3. **Repeated runs spending searches** (issue 9): leave it bounded per run,
   or stop verification once a company has been through one full pass?

## 10. Sign-off

| | |
|---|---|
| Manual tests passed | __ of 10 |
| Roles you judge wrong (MT-4.4, MT-4.6) | |
| Decisions you want changed (MT-4.8) | |
| Issues found | |
| Accepted by / date | |

| 2 | That rule first refused correct claims: "Dr. Naomi Boyd has joined Robinhood Markets, Inc. as ..." and "Since joining as Vice President of Operations, Gretchen's leadership ..." | Sentences were cut at "Dr." and "Inc."; and a given name alone was not accepted | Abbreviations no longer end a sentence; a given name ties a title unless it is followed by a different surname |

plausible claim with a real quote that does not actually support it.

## 6. Limitations

- **Coverage is set by what a site lets the tool read.** For Robinhood and
  Wise the official leadership page is closed to the fetcher. The pipeline
  does not find vice presidents or most chief officers there.
- **Verification by search did not settle any role.** It adds third-party
  evidence, which the rules rightly treat as weak.
- **Repeated runs can keep spending searches** (issue 9).
- **No personal location was found.** Leaders' locations are rarely stated
  in the sources read.
- **Biographies are thin.** Each is one or two quoted sentences. Some only
  restate the title, such as "Kristo Käärmann is the co-founder and CEO of
  Wise."
- **The gold sets are not fully blind**, and precision is provisional until
  the two unjudged roles are judged.
- **Two former roles have no end date**, because no source states one.
- **The model is not fully repeatable.** Results moved between runs: the
  Warnick sentence was returned in one run and not in another. The
  model-free recovery and the checks are what keep the stored data stable.
- **Brendan Doyle is missed.** An author line under a blog post is not
  extracted as a leader.

Please confirm or change these in manual test MT-4.8.

1. **Verification and enrichment are part of `leadership collect`**;
   `--no-verify` stops before them.
2. **A check reads at most three new pages.**
3. **A role is checked once.** It is not searched again on later runs.
4. **Stated dates and earlier titles are recovered without a model**, by
   strict sentence rules. Sentences that disagree add nothing.
5. **The title must be tied to the person** (R166), replacing the
   250-character rule for titles. The window still applies to dates and to
   "is the quote about this person at all".
6. **A biography is quoted text**, never a summary written by the model.
7. **The location search is one query per person**, made only when the held
   sources give no location.
8. **`leadership eval` measures the fixtures**, not the working database,
   when fixtures exist. `export` must be run first.
9. **Precision counts only judged roles.** Unjudged and secondary-candidate
   roles are shown and counted apart, never as correct.
10. **A gold row counts toward every group its title names**, and unit-level
    offices never match a company-wide office (your instruction).
11. **A new `checks` table** and a `location_status` column in the view.
12. **Wise's leadership page was read in a browser for the hand-check
    only**, as you did for Robinhood. The pipeline did not read it.

MT-4.3 and MT-4.5 make no outside call.

  biography; Jason Warnick is former, "ended on 2026-02-06". Decide whether
